title: UEFA says it has lost confidence in FIFA leadership after investment plan
summary: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors but drew backlash that grew every day since Tuesday's announcement.
story: Successfully stopping Gianni Infantino's FIFA plan to sell World Cup profits to private investors was the first half of a high-stakes game in global soccer politics.
The second half kicked off Saturday with what seemed a clear aim of ending Infantino's decade-long presidency.
"No option should be off the table," said European soccer body UEFA, whose president Aleksander Čeferin has led the fight against Infantino in a seismic week for FIFA.
"The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."
Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors but drew backlash that grew every day since Tuesday's announcement.
Infantino was forced to scrap the plan early Saturday after his senior adviser, who sat on a White House panel, resigned and Asia's soccer body joined Europe and North America in opposing it.
UEFA, the governing body of European soccer, issued its blistering statement hours after FIFA announced it was withdrawing its private equity plan.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," UEFA said. "We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again."

Infantino's audacious bid fell apart after UEFA's 55-member nations agreed Thursday to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions. North America's CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also said they opposed the plan.
There was also an internal revolt.

Infantino's senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, a former Goldman Sachs banker who represented the soccer body on the White House Task Force for the World Cup, resigned on Friday and urged other senior FIFA staff to speak out.

Hours later, FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour issued a statement to The Associated Press, saying FIFA staff were deceived by Infantino's lack of openness in planning the sale over recent months and that the project must not continue.

"It is the project of one person," wrote Lamour, a longtime colleague of Infantino at both FIFA and UEFA. "Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions."
Infantino had proposed spinning off FIFA's commercial businesses — including World Cups and Club World Cups for men and women — into a $20 billion subsidiary with 20% owned by private investors.
The "anchor investor," described by FIFA, is a New York-based investment firm launched by Joshua Kushner, the younger brother of U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
This tumultuous week in international soccer is at least the third time Infantino has rocked it with an ambitious plan many in the sport saw as reckless.
But the fallout from FIFA's Kushner-backed plan is the first time UEFA has acted quickly to create momentum for removing the man who was its former long-time employee.
In 2018, Infantino pushed a secretive offer of $25 billion from Japan's SoftBank to create new competitions that posed a long-term risk to continental events for clubs and national teams.
In 2021, Infantino proposed playing World Cups every two years instead of four — an idea that also angered the International Olympic Committee, where he is an elected member.
Both plans created big rifts in the sport and were eventually dropped by FIFA.
Despite the turmoil, Infantino was re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023.
The third time shapes to be different.
Nov. 18 is the deadline for candidates to enter the next presidential contest, exactly four months ahead of the vote in Rabat, Morocco, where FIFA has its African headquarters.

FIFA statutes allow Infantino one more four-year term in office. The failed spinoff venture seemed like a way to create a commissioner-like role for Infantino beyond 2031, likely paying much more than his current annual salary and a bonus deal of more than $6 million.

It would take 106 votes to ensure a majority in a contested election. Continents surely do not vote uniformly en bloc, but most of Europe's 55, plus Asia's 46 and CONCACAF's 35 FIFA members would be a solid base.

title: U.S., Israel preparing to bombard energy-related targets in Iran, sources say
summary: The U.S. and Israel plan to hit Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend, although no final decision has been made, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.
story: Washington — The United States and Israel are planning what would be one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date against energy infrastructure targets in Iran, multiple sources told CBS News, with strikes possible throughout the weekend.

There was some discussion about trying to conclude by the time financial markets open Monday because of concern about how the bombings will affect the U.S. and global economy, but an end point wasn't locked in.
The Israelis have been notified and are coordinating with the United States, according to multiple U.S. sources. The president has yet to give the final 'go' orders for the strikes, the sources said.

A joint operation would mark Israel's return to combat operations which it had halted during the U.S.-brokered truce. Iran has not hit Israel since the memorandum of understanding fell apart and the U.S. restarted combat operations in early July.
An Israeli official told CBS News: "Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran."

The military strike plan came up during President Trump's cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, according to sources briefed later. Some White House aides who focus on politics were strongly opposed, one of the sources said.
While reporters were in the room, Mr. Trump said: "We'll be hitting them very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'"
"I think we just want to win," he told the press when asked about reviving diplomacy.
Energy infrastructure including power plants and refineries would likely be targeted, two of the sources said.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement to CBS News, "As President Trump said at his cabinet meeting today, the United States will win, and Iran will not have a nuclear weapon under his watch."
Chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said the Pentagon would not comment on targets before the president makes a final decision.
"The Department of War is locked and loaded, ready to execute the President's directives at a moment's notice," Parnell said in a statement.

On Saturday, several U.S. embassies in the Middle East — including Amman, Jordan; Jerusalem; and Baghdad — issued security alerts due to "heightened tensions" and said, "Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions."
A former U.S. military official told CBS that the value of hitting energy infrastructure would be to impact the Iranian military's ability to provide services and effectively govern.

When Mr. Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met earlier this week, Netanyahu briefed him on three options for the war, including military strikes focused on land resupply routes, a senior Israeli official said. Netanyahu also met with Defense Secretary Hegseth.
The U.S. has already struck bridges in this conflict that were dual-use — used by the military and civilians — a U.S. official said.
There were high-level U.S. discussions Friday about cutting electricity across Tehran, but no decision had been made as of Friday afternoon.
Last week, Mr. Trump posted on Truth Social that he would bomb and destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill 9, injure at least 27, officials say
summary: Kyiv said the strikes had killed four people, and the city's mayor reported 15 people, including two boys aged 13 and 17, were wounded and transported to hospital.
story: Russian strikes on Ukraine's capital killed at least nine people and wounded more than two dozen others, local officials said Saturday local time, after Kyiv's mayor warned of a ballistic missile attack.
It comes after the United Nations found June was the deadliest month for civilians in Ukraine since April 2022, as Moscow ramped up its long-range strikes on towns and cities across Ukraine.
Kyiv's military administration said the strikes had killed nine people, and the city's mayor reported 27 people, including four children boys, were wounded and transported to hospital.
"Explosions in the city. Kyiv is under ballistic missile attack. Stay in shelters!" Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote earlier on Telegram.
Agence France-Presse journalists also reported hearing explosions.
More than 10 explosions were heard in a row, the journalists reported, adding that the intensity of the blasts triggered car alarms on the streets.
On Thursday, a Russian ballistic missile and drone barrage across Ukraine killed at least eight civilians, including children, and wounded dozens more.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has escalated its retaliatory strikes on Russia in recent months, partly to pressure Moscow to the negotiating table after nearly four-and-a-half years of war. Ukraine has targeted energy and logistics infrastructure.
Putin acknowledged in June that Ukrainian strikes were causing "problems" for Russia, saying they were "observing a certain shortage, but it's not critical."
Russian online retail giant Wildberries said Friday its logistics facility in Volgograd caught fire after an overnight attack — the latest in a series of strikes on the company's facilities.
Kyiv has accused the e-commerce giant — which employs thousands of people and has become a key part of the economy — of storing drone parts and helping the Russian army.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with President Trump this week for talks, as Kyiv and Moscow carried out long-range strikes.
Zelenskyy said his meeting with Mr. Trump was "good" and that they discussed the licenses for the production of Patriot missile interceptors, critical in Ukraine's efforts to combat Moscow.

Mr. Trump and Zelenskyy most recently met earlier this month on the sidelines of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization in Turkey, where Mr. Trump announced the U.S. would allow Ukraine to build its own Patriot missiles.

title: FIFA scraps its World Cup investment plan after backlash
summary: FIFA is shelving a controversial plan that would have allowed for billions of dollars in private commercial investment in the World Cup after the proposal was met with fierce opposition from its member nations.
story: FIFA, world soccer's governing body, is shelving a controversial plan that would have allowed for billions of dollars in private commercial investment in the World Cup after the proposal was met with fierce opposition from its member nations.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place," FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in a statement Friday evening.

Earlier this week, the British newspaper The Times first revealed Infantino's secret plan, called FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, under which FIFA would have created a commercial rights and event operations company, 20% of which was to be sold to private investors with FIFA retaining ownership of 80%.
FIFA had said that FFE would be given an initial evaluation of $20 billion, with $4.2 billion going to "carefully selecting long-term investors."

FIFA confirmed in an earlier statement that Thrive Eternal, a venture spearheaded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, was "expected to lead the proposed investor group." Thrive Eternal is a subsidiary of Thrive Capital, an investment firm owned by Joshua Kushner.
FIFA had estimated that under the deal, the 211 member associations of FIFA would see their so-called FIFA Forward Funding rise from $8 million per four-year cycle to approximately $20 million.
On Tuesday, a source close to Thrive Capital told CBS News that criticism of the firm's involvement was unjustified.

"I think the first assumption is that Trump was involved in FFE in any capacity, which is just not accurate," the source told CBS News. "Josh himself does not have any links with the administration, he does not have any political roles, he has not donated to them, he is not involved in any capacity. If you look at his donation record, all of the causes he has donated to are Democrat ... it's kind of unfair to assume a lot about somebody just because of what their brother does."
Asked by reporters during a Cabinet meeting Friday if FIFA officials or Infantino had spoken to him about Infantino's plan, Mr. Trump responded, "No, I never spoke to him."

The blowback from Infantino's proposal was swift. UEFA, Europe's powerful soccer federation, announced Thursday that its 55 members had agreed to boycott competitions organized by FIFA, including the World Cup, if Infantino pushed forward with his project, calling it "irresponsible and indefensible."
"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product," UEFA said. "It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies," adding that "the World Cup is not for sale."

North America's soccer governing body, the 41-member Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football, followed suit, rejecting the plan and questioning "the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history."
CONCACAF, however, stopped short of making a boycott threat.

On Friday, the Asian Football Confederation released a statement in which it didn't outright reject the plan, but said that it stood "in solidarity with UEFA and CONCACAF in expressing serious concerns over FIFA's proposal to introduce private investment into FIFA's flagship competitions and the decision-making process around FFE."
Also Friday, Carlos Cordeiro, one of Infantino's senior advisers, resigned from his post, saying in a statement that he could not "stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup."

"The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed," Infantino said Friday. "And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders."

Infantino has received mounting criticism in recent months over his close relationship with Mr. Trump leading up to the 2026 World Cup, which the U.S. hosted with Mexico and Canada. Last year, Infantino awarded Mr. Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize.

Earlier this month, during the World Cup tournament, Mr. Trump said he personally asked Infantino to review a red card that was given to U.S. striker Folarin Balogun during a knockout game against Bosnia and Herzegovina. Under FIFA rules, the red card required that Balogun be suspended for the team's next match against Belgium.

"All I did, I asked for a review because I didn't think it was a foul," Mr. Trump said at the time. "... If they wouldn't allow, you know, a top player, maybe the best, maybe among the best players on the team, I think it would have had a big stain. And I related, just that, I didn't tell him what to do, I can't tell him what to do."
In an unprecedented move, FIFA overturned Balogun's suspension just one day before the Belgium match, and without a detailed explanation.

title: Amy Schumer earns praise for sharing unfiltered bikini photos amid her weight-loss journey
summary: Amy Schumer shared new bikini photos showing her weight loss results after crediting Mounjaro and hormone therapy for perimenopause symptoms.
story: The supermodel tells Fox News Digital at The Paley Center Gala in New York the healthy habits she prioritizes in summer.
Amy Schumer is soaking up what's left of summer — and showing off the results of her recent weight loss.

The 45-year-old comedian shared a series of bikini photos on Instagram over the weekend, posing confidently in a colorful two-piece while enjoying time by the water. Schumer smiled for the camera as she relaxed waterside, offering fans a glimpse at her recent getaway.
"I never knew there would be days like this," she captioned the post. "No filter as per ushe."
HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7
Amy Schumer showed off her weight loss in a series of bikini photos over the weekend. (Getty Images; Amy Schumer Instagram)
Schumer quickly earned praise from friends and fans.
"So beautiful, Amy. Happy and thriving," actress Kate Walsh commented.
"Gorgeous," another wrote.
The actress has been open with fans about her evolving relationship with her health and body over the past two years, documenting both the highs and lows of her weight-loss journey.
APP USERS CLICK HERE TO VIEW POST

In October, Schumer took to social media to share a photo of her dramatic transformation. Schumer, who was wearing a tiny black dress and heels, was accompanied by two friends as the group enjoyed the Paul McCartney concert in Las Vegas.
Friends and fans were quick to share their thoughts, praising the actress for her progress.
'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE ISSUES WARNING ABOUT WEIGHT LOSS DRUG CRAZE
"Okay Amyyyyyy🔥" comedian Anjelah Johnson commented.
"Those legs ❤️❤️❤️" Isla Fisher wrote.
Amy Schumer shares photos from her tropical getaway. (Amy Schumer Instagram)
In March 2025, Schumer praised the effects of Mounjaro (also known as tirzepatide) in a video clip shared on Instagram with her nearly 13 million followers.

"I wanted to share and keep it 100 with you, that years ago – and yes, this is completely unsafe to be driving and making a video – years ago, three years ago, I tried Wegovy and I was like puking," Schumer said in the clip captured while she was behind the wheel.

"I couldn't handle it. I don't know if they've changed the formula or whatever… but anyway, I went on this telehealth meeting with MidiHealth, and it was cheap. I wanted to try it myself, cause I wanted to recommend it to my friends who are like nurses and teachers."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
In addition to the injectable medication, which is primarily used to treat type 2 diabetes, the "Trainwreck" star detailed a new routine which includes hormones.
"They put me on estrogen and progesterone because I realized I was in perimenopause and my symptoms of being in perimenopause have disappeared," Schumer said.
It took trial and error to find what worked for her.
Amy Schumer poses on a carpeted staircase while wearing a light cream dress, shown in both a full-body shot and a close-up portrait. (Amy Schumer/Instagram)
During an appearance on "The Howard Stern Show" last year, the comedian opened up about her scary experience trying medication for weight-loss purposes.

"I have this gene – GDF15 – which makes you extremely prone to nausea, which is why I was so sick during my pregnancy. So, I tried Ozempic almost three years ago and I was like bedridden, I was vomiting, and then you have no energy but other people take it, and they're all good," she explained.

"I lost 30 pounds so quick," said Schumer, who is mom to 4-year-old son Gene, whom she shares with ex-husband, Chris Fischer. "I looked great, and I couldn't lift my head off the pillow, so what's the point?"

Schumer has long been outspoken about body image and the pressure women face in Hollywood. Rather than shying away from criticism, Schumer has often used humor to address comments about her appearance while encouraging others to focus on their health instead of unrealistic beauty standards.
Amy Schumer admitted to suffering a medical setback during an appearance in New York with Amanda Hirsch. (Theo Wargo)

In February 2024, Schumer revealed she had been diagnosed with Cushing syndrome after fans questioned the swelling in her face. She later said she viewed the diagnosis as a blessing because it led doctors to uncover the underlying cause.

Over the years, Schumer has also been candid about living with endometriosis and undergoing a hysterectomy in 2021, frequently sharing updates about her health to help normalize conversations around women's medical issues.

title: Stephen Baldwin on choosing born-again Christianity over Hollywood after a life-changing encounter with God
summary: Stephen Baldwin reveals how a Brazilian housekeeper's prophecy and a skateboarding ministry led him to leave Hollywood after finding mega success.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Stephen Baldwin believes he could have been one of Hollywood's biggest stars, but he doesn't regret leaving the business for something far more important: his faith.

In a new interview, Baldwin, 60, reflected on the career-defining success that followed his role in the Oscar-winning 1995 crime thriller, "The Usual Suspects," and opened up about why he never felt drawn to chase stardom.

"I probably could have pointed myself in the direction of becoming a big star," Baldwin told People. "But that wasn't me. I didn't want to be Tom Cruise, and have to make $100 million at the box office. I'd rather be a schmuck from Massapequa."
HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE
Stephen Baldwin left Hollywood after finding faith. (Getty Images)
Baldwin said his priorities shifted dramatically after embracing born-again Christianity in 2001.

According to the actor, his faith journey began after he and his wife, Kennya, hired a Brazilian housekeeper who claimed she had been sent by God because the couple would one day become Christians and start a ministry.

"My wife tells me, ‘I just spoke to Augusta, and she said the real reason she’s here is because God spoke to her, and she said in the future you and I will become born-again Christians and have our own ministry,’" Baldwin told the outlet.
JD VANCE REVEALS WHAT DREW HIM BACK TO GOD AFTER SEEING CHRISTIANS HAD LIFE ‘FIGURED OUT’

At first, Baldwin admitted he was skeptical. However, after attending a handful of evangelical events with his sister — who had already become a born-again Christian — and witnessing a Christian skateboarding ministry that blended extreme sports with worship, he said everything shifted.
Brothers Alec Baldwin and Stephen Baldwin have always supported each other throughout the years. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"Down on the beach, they had built a skate park on the sand with plywood. And these funky, super committed, cool, tattooed, pierced skateboarders were there and they’d skate, stop, pick up a microphone and start preaching evangelistically, and like 5,000 kids would be around watching because of their interest in the skateboarders," he recalled. "I felt a calling."
Baldwin eventually created a skate video with a Christian message, titled "Livin' It."
FORMER SUPERMODEL SAYS CELEBRITIES NEED TO 'WAKE UP' AND RECOGNIZE CHRISTIAN FANS

"In the first six months we’d distributed 10,000 copies. Then one of the bigger churches called and asked what it would cost to bring the skaters from the video to their church for a live event. So that’s when I left Hollywood," he said. "I went to 125 churches over four years," he said. "Jesus and the Holy Spirit fascinated me."
Baldwin admitted that Hollywood hasn't always been super accepting of his religious and political outspokenness.
"I think they thought I act a little too weird," said Baldwin, who supported President Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024.

"I get a lot of DMs from people who tell me how my work has touched them and that’s all that matters. I’m happy to be where I’m now at 60. I’m so blessed. And I absolutely believe that the best is yet to come."
These days, Stephen Baldwin is enjoying being a grandfather and focusing on faith-filled projects.

Today, Baldwin says he's focused on producing faith-based films for younger audiences while hosting his podcast, "One Bad Movie," where actors discuss the worst film or filming experience of their careers.

The actor also said becoming a grandfather has only strengthened his perspective on life.
"I've done 100 movies, I've made more money than I could have wildly imagined, and I'm married to the hottest chick I've ever seen in my life," Baldwin said. "Jesus is my rock. My wife is my anchor."

title: Tom Selleck said he almost missed playing iconic role on 'Magnum, P.I.': 'It was a big fight'
summary: Tom Selleck reveals James Garner's advice that saved his career and led to a complete rewrite of the original "Magnum, P.I." script he initially hated.
story: Donnie Wahlberg says working with Tom Selleck on "Blue Bloods" showed him "there's always something more to learn."
Tom Selleck almost passed up one of his most iconic roles.

During a recent conversation with Ted Danson on his podcast, "Where Everybody Knows Your Name," Selleck explained that a conversation with fellow actor James Garner about his issues with the original script of "Magnum, P.I." ultimately convinced him to take the job.

"I'm sitting there, and I'm pretty preoccupied 'cause something had happened," Selleck told Danson. "And he says, ‘What's wrong?’ And I said, ‘Well, look, I had a contract at the studio for a series, but I fulfilled that contract. Now the studio is assigning this show to me, saying the contract is still valid and that I have to do it.’ The show, incidentally, was called ‘Magnum’ and I hated it. It was terrible."
TOM SELLECK SAYS ‘BLUE BLOODS’ CAST MADE MAJOR SACRIFICE TO SAVE THE SHOW BEFORE CANCELLATION
Tom Selleck is seen as Thomas Magnum on "Magnum, P.I." (Sunset Boulevard)
In the original script, written by Glen A. Larson of "Battlestar Galactica" and "Fall Guy," Thomas Magnum had "no flaws, and he had two beautiful women on his arm and a Ferrari."

Garner advised Selleck, "‘You don't have much power, but if they want you, you'll never have more power than you do right now. That's all I'm gonna say.’ And I said no to the studio. And Jim Garner, in a way, just kind of saved my life. I would've been long gone from that version of ‘Magnum.’"
Selleck has made similar comments in the past – in 2015, he told AARP that the original version of the character was "very James Bond-like."
He referenced Garner then, too, saying that he told the people behind the show that he'd prefer it if the character was more similar to Garner's Jim Rockford on "The Rockford Files."
James Garner of "The Rockford Files" advised Selleck on "Magnum, P.I." (NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
"I said, 'I don't want to be Rockford, but I want to do something like that, where the guy is fallible,'" he said at the time.
Selleck admitted to Danson that "it was a big fight for a long time," saying that his lawyer later told him that he would have a choice of three submissions for "Magnum, P.I."

By that time, Selleck said he had done a miniseries called "The Sacketts," "which was a huge, huge break. So they knew that I could handle a series. And so, they gave me a choice. ‘And you're gonna meet with these writers.’"
Selleck said he had never met with a writer, "And now the writers are auditioning for me."
Selleck said he wanted Thomas Magnum to have depth. (Getty Images)

He told "Magnum, P.I." co-creator Donald P. Bellisario, "I want to do something like ‘Rockford.’ I want a character with flaws and some heart.’ And he said, ‘Say no more.’ He did. And he came back in about two weeks with the best TV movie I had ever read at the time, and it was called ‘Magnum.’"
Selleck admitted to Charlie Rose in 1997 that he'd "bet the farm" by pushing back so hard on the initial script.

"They said I can’t do that, and I said ‘I know I can’t, but I’m going to, and you’ve got to change this, or I can’t do it,'" he told Rose, adding that "had it not worked out, I think I would have gotten a pretty good reputation for being difficult and never worked again. But the point was I wanted to play a flawed guy."
SCOTT EASTWOOD CREDITS HIS FAMOUS FATHER'S WORK ETHIC FOR MAKING HIM AWARE OF 'BULLS---' IN THE FILM INDUSTRY

The "Blue Bloods" star told Danson he refuses to ever call the show anything but "Magnum" because after the studio lawyers looked at it, they worried Clint Eastwood would sue over the title’s similarity to "Magnum Force," "So, we'll put a P.I. there."

"I did not like that," he said. "But we lost that battle. P.I. in Hawaii is not the most flattering term for Filipino Islander, and I was living in Hawaii at the time, and I just… so I don't call it that name, I call it ‘Magnum.’"
Tom Selleck promoting his memoir in April. (Getty Images)

At the time, Selleck said that despite his success with "The Sacketts," he had done six unsold pilots, "and I know what they were saying. They're saying, ‘Who the hell does he think he is? He's never even gotten on the air.’ So, if it hadn't worked, I would've been long gone and back with United Airlines pretty quick."
Selleck had participated in United Airlines’ management training program while studying business in college.

"But, I don't know, it was a risk. I'm not sure my dad ever said, ‘Risk is the price you pay for opportunity,’ but he lived his life that way. And this seemed to me to be the time to take a risk."

title: Princess Margaret, Lord Snowdon's country retreat on the market for first time in history at $5.3 million
summary: Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon's former getaway in the countryside is on the market publicly, for the first time in its over 500 year history.
story: Katie Nicholl, royal correspondent for Vanity Fair and co-host of "The Royals Uncensored," discusses Harry's UK security battle, the king's offer of a royal residence and growing palace frustration.
The former home of Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones, better known as Lord Snowdon's former country retreat, is on the market for the first time in the home's history.

Known as The Old House, the home, which was gifted to Lord Snowdon by his uncle, designer Oliver Messel, prior to his marriage to Princess Margaret, is listed with Blue Book Agency for about $5.3 million.
Originally built in 1481, the cottage in West Sussex came into the possession of the Messel family in 1890 and was passed down for generations before Oliver gifted it to the royal couple.

Upon receiving the 5,750-square-foot home on the 5.52-acre property, Lord Snowdon transformed the dilapidated home into a private retreat away from the public, often hosting many famous faces, including actor Peter Sellers, ballerina Dame Margot Fonteyn, Bianca Jagger, financier Sir Evelyn de Rothschild and more.
Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon's former home is on the market publicly for the first time in its over 500-year history. (John Senior Photography)
PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE’S $3 MILLION FROGMORE MAKEOVER COULD SOON BE ERASED: EXPERTS

"What Lord Snowdon created here was not simply a private home but an extraordinary creative retreat," Theo James-Wright, director at Blue Book Agency, said. "This was a place where royalty mixed with artists, actors, writers and designers, where some of the most influential figures of the 20th century gathered behind closed doors. Very few houses can genuinely claim to have witnessed such a remarkable chapter of British cultural history."
The rich history surrounding this house inspired an episode in season three of the popular Netflix series, "The Crown."
The home's entryway shows off the rustic charm of the home. (Ben Wright Photography)
The living room features multiple places to sit, as well as a unique fireplace. (Ben Wright Photography)

Some of the elements Snowdon brought to the home include a redesigned kitchen, a balcony salvaged from Ascot Racecourse's Royal Box during refurbishment works, a lake he created and a "time capsule of royal, cultural and family life" made up of newspaper clippings detailing royal scandals and major events, put together by Snowdon himself.

The estate features a main house with six bedrooms, as well as a pool house which can be used as a guest suite. In addition, the grounds include a garden office, library, tractor shed and other amenities.
The home also includes a second seating room which can be used as an office space, and features a fireplace. (Ben Wright Photography)
Another sitting room features white couches and a large ship statue. (Ben Wright Photography)
While this is the first time the home has been put on the market publicly, Snowdon did sell it privately in 2003, and the current owners purchased it off-market in 2005.
KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS

"The fact that this is the first time the property has ever been publicly offered for sale makes this a genuinely rare moment," James-Wright said. "Opportunities to acquire houses with this level of provenance, architectural significance and cultural importance simply do not come along very often."
Lord Snowdon plastered newspaper clippings about the royal family on the walls of one of the bathrooms. (Ben Wright Photography)
The kitchen and dining room are found in the same space. (Ben Wright Photography)
Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon first met in 1958, and their friendship quickly turned into a romance, with the palace announcing their engagement in February 1960.
They were married just a few months later in May 1960 at Westminster Abbey. Their wedding was the first royal wedding to be televised, attracting an estimated 300 million viewers worldwide.
The home features six bedrooms, including the spacious primary. (Ben Wright Photography)
One of the remaining features from Lord Snowdon's remodel is a lake. (Ben Wright Photography)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Over the course of their marriage, the couple welcomed two children: their son David Armstrong-Jones in November 1961, and their daughter Lady Sarah Chatto in May 1964.

They were married for 16 years before announcing their separation in March 1976, later finalizing their divorce in July 1978. Despite ending their marriage, the two are said to have remained good friends in the following years.
The home is on an over five-acre property and features manicured lawns with hedges. (Ben Wright Photography)
The backyard also features a sizable swimming pool, with a pool house that can be used as a guest suite. (Ben Wright Photography)
Following their divorce, Lord Snowdon married Lucy Lindsay-Hogg in 1978, while Princess Margaret never remarried.
Princess Margaret died in February 2002 at the age of 71 due to a stroke, after her health began to decline in the 1990s. Lord Snowdon died in January 2017 at the age of 86.

title: 'Remember the Titans' star Ethan Suplee issues warning about weight-loss drug craze
summary: Ethan Suplee warns GLP-1 weight-loss drugs aren't a "one-stop shop," saying resistance training and healthy habits are essential for lasting results.
story: Ethan Suplee shares his perspective on GLP-1 medications, arguing they offer significant health benefits but should be paired with strength training, proper nutrition and realistic expectations for lasting success.
Ethan Suplee pumped the brakes on the GLP-1 craze, warning that the wildly popular weight-loss drugs aren't the miracle fix many people believe they are.

As millions of Americans continue turning to blockbuster GLP-1 medications, Suplee said the drugs are only one piece of the puzzle. Drawing from his own decades-long weight-loss journey, the actor said sustainable success comes from building healthier habits instead of relying on medication alone.

Suplee has been candid about his decades-long battle with obesity. The "Remember the Titans" actor weighed roughly 500 pounds at his heaviest and ultimately lost around 300 pounds through years of diet and lifestyle changes. He has also undergone multiple skin-removal surgeries and now hosts weekly discussions on his show, "LifeLONG with Ethan Suplee," about long-term weight management.
MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS
Ethan Suplee said GLP-1 medications are not a "one-stop shop" for weight loss, reflecting on the habits that helped him lose roughly 300 pounds and keep the weight off. (Courtesy of Ethan Suplee)

The 50-year-old actor started dieting at just 5 years old and later, by his own volition, at age 24. "And I kind of spun my wheels for 15 years on these yo-yo diets simply because I didn't communicate," Suplee told Fox News Digital. "And when I didn't communicate to anyone else, I didn't actually figure out what I really wanted."

After decades of trial and error, Suplee said his own experience taught him there isn't a shortcut to lasting weight loss. While he acknowledged the weight-loss drugs can be an effective tool, he argued they aren't a replacement for building healthier habits.

"As a kid, I wanted a magical diet drug so badly. And now we have what is a magical diet drug," he said. "I think, unfortunately, it's also not a one-stop shop. I think you can hop on a GLP-1 and experience weight loss. You can see the scale go down week over week for a long time without having to do anything else."
"... I think when people imagine their ideal — I don't think the GLP-1s get anyone to their ideal."
'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SHOWS OFF MUSCLES AFTER DRASTIC WEIGHT LOSS TRANSFORMATION

After weighing nearly 500 pounds at his heaviest, Ethan Suplee said lasting weight loss required more than medication, emphasizing the importance of changing his relationship with food. (Phillip Faraone/WireImage)
Suplee emphasized that the medications can dramatically improve people's health and said he wouldn't discourage anyone from using them.

"By the way, a small amount of weight loss provides a huge health benefit," he added. "So if you're just going into it, going like, 'I just want to be healthier. Let me hop on this GLP-1 agonist and improve my health.' Bravo to you. You're going to do that... I'm not criticizing those people."
But Suplee said the conversation becomes more nuanced for people hoping to reach an "ideal" weight or transform their physique.

"I think for those people, just hopping on a GLP-1 is not enough," Suplee added. "I think it also will require some resistance training to preserve lean tissue... maybe increase protein a bit... I just think [they] aren't a one-stop shop."
WATCH: ‘REMEMBER THE TITANS’ STAR ETHAN SUPLEE WARNS POPULAR GLP-1 DRUGS AREN'T A CURE-ALL FOR LASTING WEIGHT LOSS
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The "My Name is Earl" star said his own experience ultimately shaped a simple philosophy: There's no single answer when it comes to long-term weight loss. He said lasting success comes from addressing the many factors that influence a person's health and relationship with food.

"I don't think it's ever going to be one thing," Suplee explained. "I think it is partially the amount of food you're consuming, partially the types of food you're consuming, partially how sedentary you are, and partially your emotional and potentially mental behavior and relationship with food."
"There's an ecosystem to everybody's life."

The "Remember the Titans" star has been candid about his decades-long health journey, saying long-term success came from honesty, consistency and healthier habits — not a quick fix. (Courtesy of Ethan Suplee)
It's a lesson Suplee said became even clearer after he reached his goal weight.
"I found maintaining weight loss to be a hell of a lot harder and more complicated than losing weight," he admitted.
Suplee said he still grapples with the same cravings he experienced before losing roughly 300 pounds.
"If I see an advertisement for McDonald's, I want McDonald's," he said. "I'm hungry. This is true today as it was 20 years ago."
WATCH: ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS WEIGHT LOSS WOULD BRING NEW EDGE TO ROLE HE'D LOVE TO REVISIT
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Before becoming known for his dramatic 300-pound weight loss, Ethan Suplee built a career with memorable roles in movies like "Remember the Titans" and as Randy Hickey on the hit comedy "My Name Is Earl." (Hopper Stone/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank)
He was quick to clarify that long-term weight maintenance isn't about completely cutting out fast food, including McDonald's.

"But it's not eating it emotionally, not eating it to cure my anxiety, not eating it out of compulsion, and then not overeating it," Suplee added. "Like, these are all the factors I have to deal with to maintain my weight."
When asked what has allowed him to maintain his weight loss over the years, Suplee pointed to a less obvious factor: learning to be honest with himself by opening up to others.

"I found I could become more honest with myself by opening up and being honest with other people," Suplee said. "And I think that really made a huge difference in my ability to maintain this weight loss as long as I have."

title: Mackenzie Phillips says 'morals clause' led to abrupt exit from 'One Day at a Time'
summary: Mackenzie Phillips reveals the lunch break confrontation that triggered her "morals clause" and ended her role on "One Day at a Time" in 1980.
story: Mackenzie Phillips told Fox News Digital at the Chiller Theatre Expo that she and Valerie Bertinelli drank wine and used cocaine together during breaks while working on "One Day at a Time."
Mackenzie Phillips is reflecting on the moment that ended her run on "One Day at a Time."
The sitcom star recently attended Fanboy Expo Knoxville in Tennessee, where she spoke about the "morals clause" in her contract and how it contributed to her abrupt departure from the series.

"One Day at a Time" made Phillips a household name alongside co-stars Bonnie Franklin and Valerie Bertinelli. Behind the scenes, however, the actress was battling addiction. The 66-year-old said her struggles with substance abuse led to additional provisions in her contract.
MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SAYS SHE AND VALERIE BERTINELLI DRANK WINE, DID COCAINE DURING SITCOM BREAKS

Mackenzie Phillips starred as Julie Cooper on the CBS television comedy series "One Day at a Time." She recently told a panel at Fanboy Expo Knoxville in Tennessee that she had a "morals clause" in her contract before her abrupt end. (CBS/Getty Images)
"We all had a morals contract, but mine was a little more specific," she said at the event, People magazine reported.
According to the outlet, the actress said that if producers suspected she was "under the influence," they would "have the right to take [me] to a doctor for urinalysis."
Mackenzie Phillips's character was written off after she was fired. (CBS/Getty Images)
Phillips said everything changed during a lunch break between scenes.
WATCH: MACKENZIE PHILLIPS REVEALS WILD COCAINE-FILLED BREAKS WITH VALERIE BERTINELLI

"One day, I was asleep on the couch," she recalled. "It was lunch hour. Everybody would just take a little nap. And [co-executive producer] Patricia Fass Palmer, who I hated for years, and now we're very good friends, she came up to me, and she said, 'Mac, wake up. Wake up. We're gonna take you to the doctor and have you pee in a cup.'"
Carly Simon, James Taylor, Mackenzie Phillips and Peter Asher attend a party at Studio 54 in New York City on April 17, 1978. (John Bright/WWD/Penske Media via Getty Images)
Phillips told the panel her first reaction was to ask for more time, knowing that "cocaine runs through your system so quickly." Palmer, however, immediately shut down the idea.
Palmer then told her it was time to leave.
The cast from "One Day at a Time," from left, Mackenzie Phillips as Julie Cooper, Bonnie Franklin as Ann Romano Royer and Valerie Bertinelli as Barbara Cooper. (CBS via Getty Images)

"She said, 'No, we're not waiting until tomorrow,'" Phillips said. "And I said, 'OK, well.' She said, 'All right, Mac. Grab your stuff and get it together. Get all your stuff. And leave.' So that's what I did. And that was that."
Mackenzie Phillips left "One Day at a Time" for good in 1983. (CBS/Getty Images)

Phillips starred in "One Day at a Time" from 1975 to 1980 before her character was written off following her firing, according to People. She later returned for a guest arc before leaving the series for good in 1983, the outlet reported.
Phillips has continued to speak candidly about her struggles with addiction in recent interviews.

Mackenzie Phillips attends The Paley Honors: A Special Tribute to Television's Comedy Legends at the Beverly Wilshire Four Seasons Hotel in Beverly Hills, on Nov. 21, 2019. (David Livingston/Getty Images)
Back in May, Phillips told Fox News Digital that one memory from her time on the show might still surprise fans today.
"Oh, I don't know. Oh, OK. So, this might surprise you — during lunch break, Valerie and I would drive to my house, get in the pool, drink wine and snort coke," Phillips said.
Phillips quickly clarified that Bertinelli has also spoken openly about that period.

MacKenzie Phillips and Valerie Bertinelli star as Julie and Barbara Cooper in the CBS series "One Day at a Time," which aired from 1975 to 1984 and followed Ann Romano and her daughters moving back to Indianapolis after a divorce. (CBS/Getty Images)
"Valerie talks about it openly, so it's not like I'm pulling her covers or anything," she said. "... Valerie didn't have the kind of addiction that I had; she didn't have addiction."
The former child star said drug use was also common behind the scenes of the sitcom.
"And you know, so we would do coke together in the dressing room and stuff," Phillips said.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
In this undated photo, Mackenzie Philips and Valerie Bertinelli present at an event. (M. Phillips/WireImage)
"I just happened to be the one that got caught. And thank God I got caught, you know?"
Asked by Fox News Digital what keeps her grounded today, Phillips pointed to her faith and perspective.
"What keeps me grounded is my faith and just knowing how strong and… empowered my history has made me," Phillips said.
Mackenzie Phillips attends the "Love Boat" cast christening of the Regal Princess cruise ship at Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on Nov. 5, 2014. (Gustavo Caballero/Getty Images)
She said people sometimes respond to her life story with pity, but that's not how she sees it.

"Someone was just saying, 'Oh my God, I feel so sorry for everything you went through,'" Phillips recalled. "And I was like, 'Don't feel sorry for me because everything I went through, even though it was horrible and difficult, made me the woman I am today.'"
WATCH: MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SAYS FAITH AND RESILIENCE HELPED SHAPE WHO SHE IS TODAY
Phillips said she does not believe she could erase parts of her past and remain the same person.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

Actress Mackenzie Phillips signs copies of her book, "Hopeful Healing: Essays on Managing Recovery and Surviving Addiction," at Barnes & Noble at The Grove in Los Angeles on Feb. 28, 2017. (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)
"If I could go back and just take this part out, then I might not be who I am," she said. "And I feel very blessed in my life."

The actress has been candid for years about addiction, trauma and recovery. Phillips is the daughter of John Phillips, co-founder of The Mamas & the Papas, and his first wife, Susan Adams. She chronicled her life in her memoir "High on Arrival" and later explored recovery in "Hopeful Healing."

Actress Mackenzie Phillips and executive producer Norman Lear arrive at the premiere of Netflix's "One Day at a Time" at The London West Hollywood at Beverly Hills in West Hollywood, on Dec. 14, 2016. (Amanda Edwards/WireImage)
During her conversation with Fox News Digital, Phillips said resilience has become central to how she views her life.
Mackenzie Phillips and her son Shane Barakan attend the opening night of "Annie" to benefit CASA of Los Angeles at the Pantages Theatre in Hollywood. (Gregg DeGuire/WireImage)

"I have a high, high resilience," she said. "You know, the love of my son, my family, my sisters — even though that relationship was very difficult for a long time — I just believe ... I have a strong faith, and, I mean, I had no choice. Be resilient or die."
Phillips has also used her recovery to help others. In addition to acting, she has worked in the addiction and recovery field, including as a counselor and manager at Breathe Life Healing Centers.
Fox News Digital's Danielle Minnetian contributed to this report.
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Carmen Electra says 'don't let anyone tell you you're too old' after Playboy return at 54
summary: Carmen Electra reveals what makes her most confident at 54 and shares advice for the new "Baywatch" cast starring Brooks Nader as a series regular.
story: Carmen Electra shares her thoughts on what it takes to keep the "spark alive" in relationships.
Carmen Electra isn't ready to hand over her sex symbol crown.
At 54, the "Baywatch" bombshell is returning to Playboy three decades after becoming one of the magazine's most iconic cover stars with a message for critics: Age isn't calling the shots.

The actress and model first appeared in the magazine in 1996 at age 24 and now graces the pages of Playboy's Summer 2026 issue, which is on sale now. Posing in fishnets, Electra also answered readers' burning questions about love.
CARMEN ELECTRA CHANNELS HER PLAYBOY PAST IN LEOPARD-PRINT BUNNY COSTUME ON THE RED CARPET
Carmen Electra is in the summer 2026 issue of Playboy, available now. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)
Electra has a message for women who think getting older means fading into the background: Don't buy it.

"Don't let anyone tell you you're too old," she told Fox News Digital. "That's a myth. You are living your own life. You're not living your life for other people. And honestly, if you're manifesting that, that's what it's going to be for you. You have to change your thought process. You have to start telling yourself every morning, 'I'm beautiful. I'm good enough. I look great. I'm pretty.' Whatever it is that you want to be, you can be that."
Carmen Electra arrives at The Abbey's 35th Anniversary at The Abbey Food & Bar in West Hollywood, on May 20, 2026. (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic/Getty Images)

"At one time in my life, I was reading a lot of books about Buddhism," she reflected. "I remember one book talked about your inner child and never losing your inner child. And I've always been a bit childish. So I always thought, 'I'm not going to lose it.' I never want to lose that, and I'm not going to. And I think the people who are older than me, who are still in this business and who I think are beautiful, have a youthful spirit. And people will love you for being who you really, truly are."
WATCH: CARMEN ELECTRA REVEALS HER SIMPLE RULE FOR KEEPING THE ‘SPARK ALIVE’ IN RELATIONSHIPS
Long before "Baywatch" turned her into a household name, Playboy introduced Electra to the world. Electra admitted she never expected to appear in the magazine again.
Carmen Electra stars as lifeguard Lani McKensie on the hit television series "Baywatch" in 1997. (Getty Images)

"I just thought, 'I'm going to go with the flow of life,'" she laughed. "But look, I figured I'm already posting sexy stuff on my Instagram page. So why not? Let's go for it. Let's do it. And it's Playboy. Playboy is so iconic. So let's do it. And I'm so happy that I did."
Electra didn't have to break into her iconic slow-motion beach run to get camera-ready. For the shoot, a walk around the neighborhood did the trick.
Carmen Electra stepped in as a Playboy advisor and answered pressing questions about love and dating. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"I try to do something every day," she said. "But I've been so busy, and we went straight into shooting. So I didn't get to prepare the way I wanted to. I really wanted to hit the gym, but I ended up taking walks in the neighborhood to make everything happen on time. But it looks so good. And I'm even happier with the reaction from everyone else out there."
Electra said she reads her DMs and that fans have flooded her with heartfelt messages following her return to Playboy.
Carmen Electra plays Celebrity Bunny Dealer at the Playboy Club at The Palms Hotel in Las Vegas, on Dec. 13, 2008. (Jon Kopaloff/FilmMagic)

"It's changed," she said. "At one time, some people were going in on me, and I'm like, 'What did I do to you?' I read everything. And I got to this place with myself where I was like, 'It's not my problem. I'm putting myself out there. If someone doesn't like what I'm doing, they have the right not to like it.'

"I came to terms with that. And once I came to terms with that, my followers changed a lot. Every once in a while, somebody will say something negative. I ignore it, whatever. For the most part, it's all about love."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Carmen Electra first appeared in Playboy in May 1996. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"I have a tattoo on my wrist that says 'love,'" she shared. "I've always been about love. I've always come from a place of love. And if we could all do that, what a wonderful place we could be in. If you really mess with me, I don't know how much love you're going to get. But I truly believe in love. And I feel it from my followers. Look, sometimes I'm trying different things on my Instagram page. Not everyone's going to love those things, and you might not get as many likes. But you turn around and boom, my fans are there."
After making a splash in Hollywood, Electra has discovered what makes her feel most confident, and it has nothing to do with looking glamorous. For her, it's being booked and busy.
Carmen Electra attends the Summer Party "La Grande Bellezza" at Restaurant Bellucci on July 9, 2026, in Berlin, Germany. (Gerome Defrance/Getty Images)

"I feel the most confident when I'm working, and I've been working a lot," she said. "When I'm working, I'm really happy. It's weird; you would think that by now I'd be over it. But I'm just not. I love it. And the more I work, the more confident I feel. When I'm in love, I feel confident. But I don't have someone in my life right now. But I'm still confident because I'm working."
Carmen Electra is in the new issue of Playboy alongside cover girl Cara Delevingne. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

These days, Electra is happy to pass the red rescue can to the new cast of "Baywatch," which is getting the reboot treatment. Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model Brooks Nader is set to star as series regular Selene.
The series was announced by Fox in 2025, nearly 25 years after the original ended in 2001.
Carmen Electra attends the "Scary Movie" global premiere at Paramount Pictures Studios on June 3, 2026, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images for Paramount Pictures)

"My advice to the ladies is to be in the best shape of your life because you're really going to be out there on the water, and you're going to be doing all of these activities," she said. "You're going to be running through the sand, diving through waves, jumping over waves and diving off boats. You're going to be doing some crazy stuff. So just get into your best shape and be ready."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Carmen Electra has racked up more than 150 covers worldwide. (Max Montgomery for Playboy)

"I also think if you're a pretty good swimmer, be an even better swimmer," she continued. "If the show is going to be anything like it was back in the '90s, it's really hard. But you know what? I did a good job. You just have to be prepared for it and enjoy the ride because it's going to be so huge, hopefully all over the world again."
Carmen Electra arrives at the world premiere of "Infinite Icon: A Visual Memoir" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles, on Jan. 20, 2026. (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic)

Because she's happiest when she's working, Electra isn't ruling out a return to the role that helped define her career. The actress said she'd love to make an appearance in the upcoming "Baywatch" reboot if given the chance.

From left: Brande Roderick, Carmen Electra and Brandy Ledford attend the premiere of "After Baywatch: Moment in the Sun" at The Bungalow in Santa Monica, California, on Aug. 26, 2024. (Michael Tullberg/Getty Images)

"Hopefully they'll think about me and bring me in for a cameo," she teased.

title: Nicole 'Snooki' Polizzi undergoes major surgery six months after her cervical cancer diagnosis
summary: Snooki's emotional video documents her hysterectomy after cervical cancer, revealing which organs doctors removed to ensure they got everything.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Nicole "Snooki" Polizzi is giving fans an update on her health, six months after sharing her cancer diagnosis.
In an emotional Instagram video shared on Saturday, the 38-year-old reality star revealed she underwent a hysterectomy six months after she was diagnosed with cervical cancer.

The video started off with clips of Polizzi arriving at the hospital and getting ready for surgery as she narrated what was going on via voice-over, before transitioning to her speaking directly to the camera following the procedure.

"I told you guys in general I’m not good with pain, and I’ve really been trying to be tough, but it’s not great," Polizzi said. "And the reason is because we did that C-section cut, and he obviously ended up taking out the uterus, my cervix and then some parts of my vagina just to make sure we get everything. So that was crazy. The fallopian tubes, all of it. We kept my ovaries so I don’t go into pre-menopause, which is nice."
Polizzi shared on Instagram that she underwent a hysterectomy six months after receiving her cervical cancer diagnosis. (Getty Images/Nicole Polizzi Instagram)
VANESSA TRUMP REVEALS BREAST CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN EMOTIONAL STATEMENT: 'I AM STAYING FOCUSED AND HOPEFUL'
The "Jersey Shore" star then cut the camera as she got emotional, telling viewers, "Sorry, it’s just been a lot," but that she is "trying to stay in good spirits."

She later shared her frame of mind prior to the surgery, explaining that the process involved hooking her up to machines, "put[ting] iodine in my nose. I had to scrub my body with this wipe, which left her feeling "nervous and anxious."

"I was starting to get nervous and anxious, getting checked in and stuff, and then they wheel me in where they’re doing the procedure," she said. "And I’m like, ‘Stay positive, it’s gonna be fine, don’t freak yourself out.’ My heart’s starting to race, I’m getting anxiety, and I’m getting the shakes. And then right when I go in, it’s just like, ‘Oh my god, like it hit me, like holy s---. I’m going under surgery. I’m losing my uterus and my cervix, fallopian tubes, half my vagina, like holy s---.’"
As she continued, she got emotional, recalling how she "start[ed] hysterically bawling" as she was "so scared," feeling like, "I don’t know what’s gonna happen."
The reality star shared she was anxious prior to the surgery but that the doctors and nurses were great. (Nicole Polizzi Instagram)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I don’t wanna feel pain," she said. "It’s very scary. But I got on the table and the nurses are great. They’re saying I’m gonna do fine. The doctors are great, so I lay down, and I’m like, ‘F---, it’s happening,’ and then they give me something in my IV to calm me down. And I’m like, What the f--- couldn’t you give me this 20 minutes ago so I could calm down?

Polizzi also shared a lighter moment in which she felt determined to "set the record" for how long she could hold out before passing out from the anesthesia after doctors told her most people only make it to three seconds, proudly telling her followers she counted to 10.

In addition to getting a hysterectomy, Polizzi shared that the doctors also treated her for diastasis recti, with the reality star saying, "Obviously, I’ve had three kids, so when you have kids, sometimes your abs, they disconnect."

When it comes to why she chose to share her health journey with her followers, she explained, "It’s a scary thing and a lot of us women deal with it, and no one really talks about it. So I’m here to give that platform for all of us ladies."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Polizzi is sharing her experience to help other women going through the same thing. (Manny Carabel/Getty Images for MTV)

"And I read a lot of your comments that some of you are going to get surgery next week, you’re doing the same thing, so I’m here to show you what’s up and it’s scary, and it’s okay to be scared," she continued. "But now it’s over. It’s over. I just have to deal with the pain. It’s just like any surgery. You have pain, you gotta manage it, manage it, get the pain meds, and in a couple of days, you’ll feel brand spanking new, no more periods. I don’t have to take birth control anymore. Hopefully I’ll be cancer free, and that’s it."
She ended her post by thanking her followers and encouraging them to "get your Pap smears, okay?"
Polizzi first shared that she was diagnosed with Stage 1 cervical cancer in February, saying at the time that  "I’m gonna probably get the hysterectomy."

title: 'The Sopranos' actor Vincent Pastore dead at 80
summary: Vincent Pastore, who played Big Pussy on "The Sopranos," has died at age 80 at his home in The Bronx, his manager Robert Attermann confirmed.
story: Retired FBI agent Séamus McElearney details the arrest and cooperation that cracked the DeCavalcante crime family and exposed the real-life inspiration for "The Sopranos."
"The Sopranos" star, Vincent Pastore, died at the age of 80.
The actor's manager, Robert Attermann, confirmed his death to Fox News Digital, saying, "Vinny passed away either yesterday or today at home in The Bronx."

"I had the privilege of representing Vinny for more than 30 years, long before 'The Sopranos' made him a household name," Attermann said. "To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable 'Big Pussy,' but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more."
Pastore was known for his role as Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on the hit HBO Max show, and played a major role as a member of Tony Sopranos clique, before betraying him.
"The Sopranos" star, Vinny Pastore, died at the age of 80. (Richard Corkery/NY Daily News Archive via Getty Images)
'TOP GUN: MAVERICK' ACTOR JAMES HANDY'S FINAL MOMENTS REVEALED IN AUTOPSY REPORT
In addition to his role on "The Sopranos," Pastore also appeared in "Goodfellas," "A Bronx Tale," "Carlito's Way," "Gotti," ""Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn," "Mickey Blue Eyes" and others.

He also appeared in a number of television projects, including "Blue Bloods," "Law & Order," "General Hospital," "Bull," "Pair of Kings," "Hawaii Five-0" and most recently lent his voice on an episode of "Yellowjackets."

"He loved being an actor," Attermann said. "He was passionate about his craft and was always encouraging, respectful, and generous with young actors, taking the time to offer guidance and support whenever he could."
Pastore also competed on a number of reality competition shows, including "Dancing with the Stars," "Celebrity Fit Club" and "Celebrity Apprentice."
Pastore rose to fame as a key character in "The Sopranos." (Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Attermann referred to Pastore as "one of the kindest, most generous people I have ever known," adding, "He treated everyone with warmth and respect, never turning down a fan who wanted a photograph or an autograph."

"He genuinely appreciated the people who supported him and always made them feel valued," he said. "For me, losing Vinny is deeply personal. Over more than three decades, I had the honor of watching not only his remarkable career but also the incredible person he was. I will miss his friendship, his loyalty, his humor, and his generosity."

He continued: "My deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and the countless fans whose lives he touched. He leaves behind a legacy that extends far beyond his memorable performances. He will be greatly missed and never forgotten. May his memory be a blessing."
Pastore's former co-stars, including Kathrine Narducci and Lorraine Bracco took to Instagram to share their own tributes to the fallen star.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Pastore is survived by his daughter Renee. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
Bracco reposted a photo of the actor on her Instagram story, writing, "Such a funny & charming man…just a beautiful soul. Absolutely heartbreaking."

Narducci shared a photo of the two of them on her feed, captioning the post, "This one is crushing , With the most heavy heavy heart I lost my Dearest Big brother friend Vincent Pastore . 35 years of friendship . This is a tremendous loss."

Micheal Imperioli, who played Christopher Moltisanti on the hit drama series, also paid tribute to the actor, sharing a photo of the two of them on the red carpet, in which Pastore has his arm around him.

"Our beloved friend and collaborator VINCENT PASTORE has passed away," he wrote in the caption. "This is a hard one for us, it seems like I’ve known Vinny forever. We did lots of work together and traveled all over the USA as well as Italy and Australia. Lots of good times. Lots of laughs. Vinny was a kind hearted brother who cared deeply about his family and friends. I will miss him always.
Imperioli paid tribute to Pastore on Instagram. (KMazur/WireImage)

Joe Pantoliano shared a few photos of the two of them together on Instagram as well, writing, "God bless him. He made it to 80.""Vin and I were never actually on set together, but through our Sopranos family I got to know him over the years." he wrote. "I always liked him. He had this incredible appetite for the business and he never lost that spark. That always made me smile. My heart goes out to his family, his friends and everyone who loved him. Rest easy, Vin. ❤️"
Pastore is survived by his daughter Renee.

title: ‘Home Improvement’ star Jonathan Taylor Thomas makes rare appearance in reunion photo with co-stars
summary: The rare "Home Improvement" cast reunion photo captures Jonathan Taylor Thomas in one of his few public appearances since stepping away from fame.
story: "Home Improvement" star Richard Karn tells Fox News Digital how co-star Zachery Ty Bryan being a child star may have led to DUI and domestic violence arrests.
Jonathan Taylor Thomas is back in the spotlight — at least momentarily.
The former child star appeared in a rare reunion photo with his "Home Improvement" co-stars Patricia Richardson and Taran Noah Smith.

Patricia Richardson sparked a wave of nostalgia when she shared a rare reunion photo with her former "Home Improvement" sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas and Taran Noah Smith, more than 25 years after the beloved sitcom ended.
‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’ STARS TIM ALLEN, RICHARD KARN REUNITE FOR NEW COMPETITION SERIES ‘ASSEMBLY REQUIRED’
"My other boys," Richardson captioned the snapshot with a heart emoji.

For eight seasons of the hit comedy series, Richardson played Jill Taylor, the wife of Tim Allen's character, Tim "The Toolman" Taylor. Thomas and Smith became household names, playing sons Randy and Mark Taylor, respectively, while Zachery Ty Bryan portrayed oldest son Brad.
"Home Improvement" cast Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Patricia Richardson and Taran Noah Smith pose for a rare photo. (Patricia Richardson / Instagram )
The reunion offered fans a rare glimpse of Thomas, who largely stepped away from Hollywood after becoming one of the biggest child stars of the 1990s.

Thomas rose to fame as Randy Taylor on "Home Improvement" and became a major teen heartthrob, appearing in films including "Tom and Huck" and "Man of the House." He also voiced young Simba in Disney’s 1994 blockbuster "The Lion King."
But at the height of his fame, Thomas made a surprising decision to walk away.
"I'd been going nonstop since I was 8 years old," Thomas told People in 2013. "I wanted to go to school, to travel and have a bit of a break."

Pictured left to right: Taran Noah Smith, Patricia Richardson, Jonathan Taylor Thomas and Zachery Ty Bryan. (Ron Galella, Ltd / Ron Galella Collection; ABC Photo Archives / Disney General Entertainment Content)
Thomas left "Home Improvement" during its eighth and final season, with his character moving to Costa Rica.

Although he largely stayed out of the spotlight, Thomas briefly returned to acting, reuniting with TV dad Tim Allen on "Last Man Standing" from 2013 to 2015. He appeared in four episodes and directed three.
Smith also left acting behind after "Home Improvement" wrapped in 1999.

"Home Improvement" cast gallery. Shoot date: July 23, 1992. Left to right: Zachery Ty Bryan, Taran Noah Smith and Jonathan Taylor Thomas. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
PATRICIA RICHARDSON SAYS CHEMISTRY WITH TIM ALLEN MADE HER TAKE THE PART ON ‘HOME IMPROVEMENT’

The former child star went on to explore a series of unexpected careers, including creating a vegan food company, working as an installation artist and helping develop energy-efficient water purification systems used overseas.

His post-Hollywood years also came with controversy. Smith married Heidi Van Pelt at 17, when she was 16 years older, and the couple divorced in 2007. He later became involved in a legal battle with his parents over control of his reported $1.5 million trust fund before eventually reconciling with his mother.
The "Home Improvement" reunion also comes as fans continue celebrating the show's legacy — and the chemistry between Allen and Richardson that helped make it a 1990s television staple.

"Home Improvement" cast gallery in July 23, 1992. Left to right: Taran Noah Smith, Patricia Richardson, Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Tim Allen and Zachery Ty Bryan. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
Richardson previously told Fox News Digital that Allen deserved more recognition for his acting abilities during the show's run.
"People don't give Tim enough credit for the acting that he was doing," Richardson said.
"He had never acted before. He was getting acting lessons on the side."
Meanwhile, Zachery Ty Bryan, who played oldest son Brad Taylor, went on to appear in projects including "Buffy the Vampire Slayer," "Veronica Mars" and "The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Bryan has faced multiple legal issues in recent years. In early 2026, he was sentenced to 16 months behind bars after pleading guilty in connection with a 2024 DUI arrest.

Decades after "Home Improvement" ended, the reunion photo brought fans back to the Taylor household — and reminded them of a cast whose lives took very different paths after leaving one of the biggest sitcoms of the '90s.
Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Henry Winkler dishes on the 'Happy Days' guest star who had a big ego
summary: Henry Winkler revealed which "Happy Days" guest star rubbed him the wrong way by repeatedly bragging about fan mail on the ensemble-driven set.
story: Henry Winkler says the older generation holds wisdom, and that’s how he learned a lot of lessons too.
Henry Winkler is sharing which former screen partner didn't leave the best impression on him.

While appearing at a recent fan expo in Tennessee, the 80-year-old actor spoke about the comradery on set of "Happy Days," explaining "on our set, there was no stardom," and how one guest star failed to mesh with the rest of the cast.

"We were an ensemble. We worked hard at making it funny every week," he said. "One guy came on as a guest star, and then he was brought back a few times, and he would mention his fan mail, and I said, ‘You don’t want to talk to me about fan mail, I got 50,000 letters a week.’"
He then explained to the actor that "we don't talk about that on the set" and that "we are all here as one."
HENRY WINKLER SAYS AMERICA DOESN'T EMBRACE OLDER GENERATION LIKE OTHER COUNTRIES DO
Winkler revealed the reason why one guest star didn't mesh well with the rest of the cast on the set of "Happy Days." (HEIDI GUTMAN/American Broadcasting Companies, Inc. via Getty Images)

Despite the warning, Winkler said the actor "kept doing it," later calling the guest star "an a--back." While he didn't name names, he mentioned that the character the actor portrayed was named Eugene.

Winkler played Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on the hit sitcom throughout all of its 11 seasons, from 1974 to 1984. After getting his big break on the show, he went on to enjoy a successful career in both film and television, earning a Golden Globe nomination for "Heroes," and starring in "The Waterboy," "Holes" and "Click."
After years in the industry, Winkler is still having new experiences on set, as he recently filmed his first nude scene for the first episode of the third season of "Loot."

"Maya Rudolph is one of my favorites. She is [a] brilliant person and a lovely person. So, when she asked me to be on the first episode of the third season of 'Loot,' I didn't even ask to read the script," he explained.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Winkler got his big break playing Fonzie on "Happy Days" from 1974 to 1984. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
He then explained that when he went to his first costume fitting, he was shocked to find "a silk robe that went to there," he said while pointing to his upper thigh. "There was nothing else."

"And then we did it in January on the beach. And I want to say the wind came from every direction," he said. "Parts of my body, large and small. … It was so cold. I was in shock. But then I was with Maya and her wonderful cast."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
While he won two Golden Globe Awards for playing Fonzie, Winkler didn't win his first Emmy Award until 2018, when he was rewarded for his work on the hit show "Barry."
He starred on the show as Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself striking a friendship with a wanted assassin, played by Bill Hader, for four seasons.
Winkler won his first Emmy Award in 2018 for his role in "Barry." (Leon Bennett/Getty Images)
"Be yourself, be honest about your ability, prepare so that you are not a flash in the pan," he said backstage after his win, per Variety.
"When I first started here in Hollywood … I thought of myself as a tree or sapling. I planted. I wanted to grow and be strong until I couldn’t do this anymore. And what a great tree it is."

title: 'Wonder Woman' star Lynda Carter stuns fans with age-defying Instagram photos of her in a bathtub
summary: Lynda Carter, 75, stunned fans with Instagram photos from the "Super Troopers 3" set, including a playful bathtub scene that sparked age-defying praise.
story: "Wonder Woman" star Lynda Carter spoke with Fox News Digital alongside Rep. Nicole Malliotakis, R-N.Y., about the bipartisan effort to build the Smithsonian American Women’s History Museum.
"Wonder Woman" star, Lynda Carter, shocked fans with her age-defying appearance on social media.
The 75-year-old actress stunned in a series of photos shared on Instagram on Tuesday, July 28, while promoting her latest project, "Super Troopers 3."

"@supertroopers Ride Again!!! Follow them and us (returning cast) For a fantastic road romp!!" she captioned the post. "But....wait for it...the last scene! I'm naked in a bathtub???? Oh noooo, @jaychandreskhar you promised not to show that!"

In one of the photos, Carter is all smiles as she lies outside in a bathtub, with bubbles covering her chest and an elegant updo. Behind Carter is a picturesque view of a lake and greenery, and a martini is seen on a table next to her.
Carter shared photos of her in a bathtub on set of "Super Trooper 3." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Axios | Live Nation)
'80S ICON KRISTY MCNICHOL MAKES RARE APPEARANCE 25 YEARS AFTER LEAVING HOLLYWOOD
Other photos show the "Supergirl" actress posing with her arms around her co-stars and crew members on the film in a gray robe.

"My God, is she getting younger?!😍" one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "Still absolutely gorgeous 😍, while a third fan chimed in adding, "Can't wait! And @reallyndacarter you look amazing!! You don't age!! ❤️🔥🔥"
Carter shared behind the scenes photos from the set of "Super Trooper 3." (Lynda Carter Instagram)

When speaking to People in March 2024, Carter shared her secret to looking youthful in her 70s, telling the outlet, "People still recognize me all the time as Wonder Woman," adding that since she hasn't "cut" her face, "I probably look just myself, but older."

"And the reason I've never had any facial surgery is just because I'm afraid. It's scary, because we've all seen some bad ones," she said. "That outcome is spending time in a chair with some really good people doing your hair and makeup."
Carter said most celebrities look like regular people without their hair and makeup done. (DREW ANGERER/AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
She explained that while most "actors and celebrities always look so great when they're on the red carpet," they often look like everyday people without makeup on and when wearing regular clothes.

"If everyone did a three-hour makeover before they left the house, then they'd all look amazing," she said. "What I'm trying to say is, there's a lot of effort behind those pictures. Don't think they walk out the door looking like that!"

Carter rose to stardom with her career-defining role playing Wonder Woman in the eponymous show, from 1975 to 1979. Decades after the show went off the air, fans continue to associate Carter with the iconic character, but she says she doesn't mind.
When speaking with E! News in October 2016, Carter explained that speaking about the show has never been an issue for her.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Carter rose to stardom playing the titular character in "Wonder Woman." (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

"I love the character. I love her. I think she stands for so much…I've heard so many great stories," Carter said. "She became so much more than this show or the comic book or the movie, she became a symbol for the beauty and the strength and the loving kindness and the wisdom of women…and gay men."
