title: Talking Shop (and travel essentials) with Brian Kelly, a.k.a. The Points Guy
summary: The Points Guy Brian Kelly is the top travel expert. He shares his essentials for every trip, including how he keeps his toddlers entertained on long flights.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

No one embodies that title of “travel expert” quite like Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy. He’s been to every continent (multiple times, including with his toddlers) and more countries than most people visit in a lifetime. But that’s not even the most impressive part: Kelly is so well-versed in credit cards, points, miles and loyalty programs that he can book flights, hotels, excursions and more for free with his eyes closed. And for the past 16 years, he’s made it his mission to teach you how to do the same.

“I want people to have confidence traveling,” says Kelly, who took The Points Guy from a personal blog in 2010 to a multi-million dollar media company today. “I want them to be better informed and have a sense of how to navigate the system because it’s overwhelming, especially if you’re a novice traveler.”

Kelly’s role at The Points Guy has changed over the years, but at its core, it’s always revolved around helping people navigate what he calls “the complicated travel landscape.” Online, on social media and in his bestselling book, “How to Win at Travel,” Kelly shares tips about how to affordably upgrade all parts of a travel experience, and educates people about issues impacting the travel industry and what that means for upcoming trips.

Kelly’s biggest travel tip these days? Embrace flexibility, especially if you’re on a budget. “There are travel deals out there, but it’s not about booking on a Tuesday or using an IP blocker,” he says. “You need to think creatively and be flexible with dates and your destination.”

Between Kelly’s most recent adventures, I talked to him about the essentials he never forgets to add to his suitcase, how he keeps his kids entertained on flights (including to Antarctica) and the safety device he wishes more people traveled with when staying in rental homes. Read more below.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Pak Reve Voyager Pak Family Passport Case
Kelly usually isn’t a solo traveler. His sons, ages 3.5 years old and 17 months, often go on trips with him — in fact, his youngest traveled to all seven continents by the time he was 12 months old.

To keep his family organized while going through the airport, Kelly puts everyone’s passports in this case, which has dedicated spots for different things. It also has a pen holder (Kelly keeps a pen on him at all times to make filling out forms easier) and slots for essentials like cash. “The world is more credit card-friendly, but especially while traveling internationally, having local currency and being able to tip is important,” says Kelly. “I believe in travel karma: treating people well who treat you well. That’s why I tip housekeeping at the beginning of my hotel stay, not at the end. That could dramatically improve the quality of your stay.”
Apple iPad Pro 11” (M5)

“I like to control my environment, so I always bring [my own] in-flight entertainment,” says Kelly. “Usually that’s on my iPad, which I put preloaded, downloaded content on.” Kelly also uses his iPad to plan trips. His favorite free online tool is Google Flights’ Explore. “If you’re flexible with your dates and destination, you can just say, ‘Hey, I want to get away for a weekend in September; show me where all the deals are,’” he says. “Technology is how you stay on top of it.”
Bose QuietComfort Headphones

Kelly has used these over-ear headphones to drown out noise on planes for years. They connect to his iPad and iPhone via Bluetooth, and they get up to 24 hours of battery life, which is ideal for long flights. He can also comfortably wear them for hours because they have plush ear cushions and a padded band.
On Cloud 6

“I love On Clouds,” says Kelly when I asked him about his favorite travel shoes. “For the airport, I wear a pair of white On Clouds that will look nice with slacks so I can wear them to casual dinners on my trip, and I can go to the gym in them and slip them on during the day.”
RØDE Wireless Micro

“I’m a big iPhone guy,” says Kelly. “I’ve gotten GoPros in the past, but especially while traveling with kids, I do most of my content on my iPhone. I like to use microphones, like Rode’s. They’re a really great way to elevate your content on the go and they’re easy to clip on.”
Grüns Kids

To entertain his kids while traveling, Kelly brings new toys and books to make the trip exciting, but the most important thing of all is snacks… lots of them. He and his sons are fans of Grüns’ superfood gummies, which come in kids’ and adult versions. “It’s a nice little sweet spike to just get that burst of energy when you’re tired from traveling, and they’re healthy,” says Kelly. He throws Quest’s protein peanut butter cups and SmartSweets in his bag, too.

Kelly’s other must-have while traveling with kids is a change of clothes for the whole family. “There will be delays, and there will be accidents,” he says. “It’s a matter of planning for the worst and hoping for the best.”
Kidde AA-Battery Powered CO Alarm (COBDL10)

“Since I travel with my kids, safety is a huge focus for me — it’s also one of the top questions I get asked,” says Kelly. “I take Kidde’s carbon monoxide alarm with me whenever I’m traveling, especially internationally, because it’s small, it slips into your bag and it’s battery operated, so it’s good for TSA.” (You have to take the batteries out in transit and insert them when you get to your destination.)

Kelly, who partnered with the brand to promote its Destination Safety campaign, also appreciates that this CO alarm detects low levels of carbon monoxide, which children are more vulnerable to, according to the brand.

title: Truth Social launches service selling faster access to Trump posts
summary: Wall Street firms can now be alerted of the “most market-moving” social media posts from President Donald Trump before the general public — as long as they pay the right price.
story: Wall Street firms can now be alerted of the “most market-moving” social media posts from President Donald Trump before the general public — as long as they pay the right price.

The service went live Saturday: a subscription to his social media platform, Truth Social, that allows financial firms and other organizations to get alerts for new posts made by Trump and other top accounts before general users do.

Trump Media and Technology Group, which owns the platform, launched the new high-speed data feed called “Truth API,” describing it as giving firms “a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform’s most market-moving Truths.”

Trump, who has the largest following on the platform by far with 13 million followers, has used Truth Social as his go-to platform to release official statements throughout his second term, including to announce that he was imposing sweeping new tariffs or to declare major military operations.

Trump’s unprecedented use of social media to reveal updates on global affairs and economic policy has contrasted sharply with prior presidents, who generally made such announcements through more formal avenues, such as through the White House press office and the official White House website.

Many trading firms already plug into Trump’s posts through Bloomberg, Reuters or other services that scrape his posts and relay them in real time to their customers. But using this data feed on Truth Social could enable firms to access his posts seconds or even milliseconds faster than the general public.
For a high-frequency trading firm, even milliseconds could make a huge difference.

The president also stands to profit from the new service. Trump is a major stakeholder in TMTG, owning 114.75 million shares to represent 41% of the company, according to his 2025 financial disclosure.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Adam Schiff, D-Calif., have urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether Trump Media is violating the law by selling faster access to the president’s posts.

The senators wrote that the subscription “appears to be an outrageous abuse of the President’s office for his personal benefit that undermines everyday investors and the integrity of our markets, while enriching Wall Street and other wealthy insiders.”
In its announcement of the new service last month, TMTG emphasized Truth Social’s impact on the market.

“Markets already move on Truth Social posts,” Kevin McGurn, interim chief executive officer of TMTG, said in a press release. “Truth API delivers a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform’s most market-moving Truths while advancing our strategy to monetize proprietary assets through a high-margin, recurring revenue stream.”
Trump launched Truth Social in early 2022 after he had been banned from X, formerly known as Twitter, and other social media platforms in 2021 following the attacks on the Capitol on Jan. 6.
Elon Musk reinstated Trump’s access to X in November 2022 shortly after he took over the platform as CEO. Trump also regained access to Facebook and Instagram in January 2023.

title: Troy Jackson launches first general election ad in Maine Senate race
summary: Maine’s Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson is launching his first general election ad, highlighting his own background as a labor organizer and going after Republican Sen.
story: Maine’s Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson is launching his first general election ad, highlighting his own background as a labor organizer and going after Republican Sen. Susan Collins.
The 30-second spot, narrated by Jackson, is backed by a seven-figure buy slated to begin airing statewide next week, his campaign told NBC News on Saturday.

“I’m a fifth-generation logger and the son of a public school teacher. My dad would work 16-hour days, and that still wasn’t enough. So when they tried to replace us with foreign labor, I led a blockade of the border,” Jackson says in the ad. “Susan Collins didn’t help us then, and she’s certainly not helping us now. We’re all getting crushed out here. Healthcare, housing, heat.”
“We’ve gotta fight back. We’re all hungry for it. Maine is ready for a change,” Jackson concludes.
The new ad points to Jackson’s strategy against Collins: paint her as a part of an establishment that is failing struggling Mainers.

It comes one week after Jackson accepted his party’s nomination for the seat at a convention in Bangor, replacing Graham Platner, who won the June primary but dropped out after a former girlfriend’s allegation of sexual assault, which he denied.

Collins, who was first elected in 1996, is running for a sixth term. She is campaigning as a moderate who brings money home to Maine, pointing to her chairmanship of the Appropriations Committee, and as someone who’s sometimes willing to break with President Donald Trump and her party’s leaders.
Maine, a blue-leaning state, represents one of the best pickup opportunities for Democrats, who need a net gain of four seats to capture control of the Senate.

title: Read The Sweet Anniversary Message James Van Der Beek’s Wife Shared, 6 Months After His Death
summary: James Van Der Beek’s wife posted a sweet message in honor of the couple’s wedding anniversary, following the actor’s death earlier this year.
story: James Van Der Beek’s wife posted a sweet message in honor of the couple’s wedding anniversary, following the actor’s death earlier this year.

Kimberly Van Der Beek took to Instagram Aug. 1 to share a moving message about her husband amid their 16th wedding anniversary. The actor, best known for starring as Dawson Leery in the coming-of-age television drama “Dawson’s Creek,” died in February.

“16 years ago I was the luckiest woman in the world to marry @vanderjames,”  Kimberly Van Der Beek wrote in the post. “The beauty of this marriage continues to unfold everyday with all these incredible children we have.”
The two got married in 2010 and had six children together: Olivia, Joshua, Annabel, Emilia, Gwendolyn and Jeremiah.

The actor, who’s also known for his roles in films “Varsity Blues” and “The Rules of Attraction,” announced in November 2024 that he had been diagnosed with colorectal cancer.  He died after a two-and-a-half-year battle with the disease.
In the post, Kimberly Van Der Beek said that her husband “continues to be present and guide us.”
“I’m eternally grateful. 🙏🌹😍🥰” she wrote.
The message was met with an outpouring of support from friends and fans, who marveled at the pair’s relationship.
“Your love set the bar for us all. Love you so much,” commented actor Jamie-Lynn Sigler, best known for her role in “The Sopranos.”
Several others wrote that the couple were “true soul mates.”
Kimberly Van Der Beek has been open about both her grief and the memories she’s had of her marriage. On June 21, she shared how she continued to feel her husband’s presence.
“Missing you so much and thinking of how magnificent you were in every single way today,” she wrote in an Instagram post. “And somehow, from the other side? You continue to parent. You’re a marvel.”

title: Zendaya Praises Husband Tom Holland’s Commitment To ‘Spider-Man’ As A Role Model
summary: Zendaya and Tom Holland are once again clearing the cobwebs of our hearts.
story: Zendaya and Tom Holland are once again clearing the cobwebs of our hearts.

In an interview with Rotten Tomatoes posted July 30, Zendaya praised Holland, her husband, while sharing her “favorite part” about his version of iconic superhero Spider-Man. The pair, who both star in the latest film “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” have been promoting the Marvel movie, which is currently in theaters.

“My favorite thing about Tom’s Spider-Man is how Tom handles Spider-Man outside of ‘Spider-Man,’” said Zendaya, who plays the snarky MJ Watson, Spidey’s love interest in the Marvel franchise. “So many people connect to this character, to Peter Parker’s Spider-Man, and especially young people, especially children, and I think that he’s just handled that weight with such grace.”

Holland is one of three main live-action actors in history to play the role on film, with Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield being the two others.  He first appeared as Spidey in the Marvel Cinematic Universe during 2016’s “Captain America: Civil War.” The next year, he headlined “Spider-Man: Homecoming.”

While Zendaya entered the franchise as MJ during Holland’s first solo feature film, her character didn’t become the superhero’s love interest until the sequel, “Spider-Man: Far From Home,” which was released in July 2019.
In the Rotten Tomatoes interview, Zendaya added that Holland “really loves and cares so much about the character and what the character means to other people.”
She explained that the role comes with the responsibility of knowing, “when you are in front of these kids, you are Spider-Man.”
“You are this person to them,” she said, turning to a clearly bashful Holland. “I just love seeing what and how you carry Spider-Man through your life in real life.”

The Marvel franchise holds a special significance for the couple. They met on the set of Spider-Man: Homecoming in 2016. And while rumors swirled for some time that they had been seeing one another, the two finally went public in September 2021 when Holland shared a post in celebration of Zendaya’s birthday.
“My MJ, have the happiest of birthdays. Gimme a call when your up xxx” he wrote.
The two were suspected to have gotten married sometime in 2025 or early 2026. And Holland finally confirmed their marriage to Esquire in a June interview.
“For me, I found my person,” he told the outlet. “She’s my best friend, and I’m the happiest I have ever been when I’m with her, but I have also never felt so supported and safe, ever. Period.”

Earlier this summer, the pair were both featured in the Christopher Nolan blockbuster film “The Odyssey,” with Holland playing titular character Odysseus’ son Telemachus, and Zendaya portraying the goddess Athena.

title: ‘Wonder Man’ Showrunner Responds To Fan Outrage After Shocking Cancellation Of Marvel Show
summary: Andrew Guest, head writer for “Wonder Man,” posted a video on TikTok August 2, sharing his thoughts on the cancellation. Guest told fans in the clip that he feels “how you all feel.”
story: After fans unleashed their disappointment at the news that Marvel canceled the critically acclaimed show “Wonder Man,” just months after the studio had renewed it, its showrunner spoke out.
Andrew Guest, head writer for the superhero show, posted a video on TikTok August 2, sharing his thoughts on the cancellation. Guest told fans in the clip that he feels “how you all feel.”

“The production was supposed to begin early next year, and there was a decision made internally between Disney and Marvel that this didn’t make sense for them, even though a few months ago it did,” Guest said. “That’s essentially all I really know.”
Marvel did not respond to multiple TODAY.com requests for comment.

Fans have been shocked by the cancellation of the show, which debuted to overwhelmingly positive reception in January. By March, Marvel surprised viewers by announcing that the show would be returning for a second season. However, reports began to circulate July 30 that the studio had reversed course. The show’s star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, who played main character Simon Williams, confirmed the reports in an Instagram post.
“Canceling ‘Wonder Man’ after already giving it the green light AND after Yahya’s Emmy nom is a huge slap in the face,” one fan wrote on X.
Another fan mourned the show, saying that they “don’t think I’ve ever felt more seen than watching Wonder Man.”
“That first season is so special to me and seemed like the perfect show for Marvel to run for years to come. It feels like robbery to not get another season,” the fan wrote.

In the TikTok video, Guest cleared any confusion, underscoring that the pivot was “not a marketing stunt” and that the decision had nothing to do with scheduling. In fact, Guest said, he had already written the first episode and shared that the writer’s room had been scheduled to begin “this month.”
“We had an outline for where the season would go, and everyone felt really good about it,” he said. “It was going to be a really incredible season that hopefully surpassed season one.”
Guest also acknowledged the online chatter around the cancellation.

Some fans have criticized Marvel for failing to support Black-led projects. Recently, Mahershala Ali opened up about his once-proposed film “Blade.” He told GQ in an interview released July 31 that the studio did not want to move forward with the project, despite having teased it at Comic-Con in 2019.

“I appreciate everybody getting out there and letting your voices be heard about how you feel about this,” Guest said in his video. “I think there’s important conversations being had online about the kind of stories that we’re prioritizing and the kind of shows platforms want to make.”
Guest added: “I hope people are listening.”
He also praised Abdul-Mateen for his performance, which landed him an Emmy nomination for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series.
“I also hope that Emmy voters are thinking about Yahya and how much he deserves an Emmy for the incredible work he did on this show,” Guest said.
Abdul-Mateen also recently responded to the update, thanking fans for their support of the project.

“Everything will shake out,” Abdul-Mateen wrote in an Instagram post. “I wanted to say thank you to everybody who WATCHED the show, ENJOYED the show, and SHARED that they enjoyed the show in some way or other.”
He concluded the social media post with a pretty perfect mic drop.
“Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the EMMYS. 🫡✌🏾” he wrote.

title: 1st Women’s Pro Baseball League Game Includes National Anthem Blunder, Iconic First Pitch
summary: The opener of the inaugural Women’s Pro Baseball League season on Aug. 1 included a National Anthem blunder and a memorable ceremonial first pitch.
story: The opener of the inaugural Women’s Pro Baseball League season on Aug. 1 had no shortage of memorable moments.

The New York Heights and the Los Angeles Queens kicked off the historic season at Robin Roberts Stadium in Springfield, Illinois. The game itself, which ended in a 10-8 come-from-behind victory by the Queens, was filled with plenty of action. It also marked the debut of the first women’s professional baseball league in the U.S. in almost three decades.
But two particular parts of the night drew a flurry of internet chatter: a rather creative rendition of the National Anthem and a moving first pitch that deserves a spot in history books.
The National Anthem, led by Motown legend Martha Reeves, drew criticisms and a whole lot of shock from social media users.
“Absolutely nothing could have prepared me for the national anthem at the first Women’s Pro Baseball League tonight,” wrote one X user.
During the performance, several players were caught on camera, attempting to keep straight faces. The shaky notes were also met with smiles and stifled laughter from those in the crowd.

Some even joked that the singer may actually have dethroned Fergie for the most, uh, interesting rendition of the song. Fergie went viral in 2018 for her slower, jazzier version of the “Star Spangled Banner” at the NBA All-Star Game.
Reeves did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.

The performance doesn’t necessarily reflect Reeves’ legendary career. The 85-year-old has long been known as the lead singer of 1960s popular Motown girl group Martha and the Vandellas. With hits like “Dancing in the Street,” “Nowhere to Run” and “(Love Is Like A) Heat Wave,” the group’s popularity and impact on music landed them a spot in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. They were inducted in 1995 by members of the B-52s.
The day of baseball, however, picked up with a moving moment from 99-year-old Maybelle Blair, who threw out the first ceremonial pitch.

Blair played in 1948 for the Peoria Redwings of the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League, the original professional women’s baseball league in the U.S.  The AAGPBL — which kicked off in 1943, flourishing during wartime, and inspiring the 1992 film “A League of Their Own” — dissolved in 1954. Blair spent decades, advocating for women’s sports.
Seated in a wheelchair, Blair threw out the pitch to Kelsie Whitmore, captain of the San Francisco Firebells.
The moment was an emotional one for many fans, who’ve waited quite some time to see women take the baseball diamond professionally.

“tears in my eyes at maybelle blair at the age of 99 getting to see another professional women’s baseball league start after so many years, the woman is a trailblazer and an icon,” one social media user said.
Another fan wrote that “seeing da new players interact w  maybelle blair makes me want to cry.”
Blair was also honored with a mascot in her likeness.
The league was first announced in 2024 by WPBL co-founder Justine Siegal. By October 2025, the league unveiled Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York and Boston as the first cities to have teams.

The first game, between the Queens and the Heights, ended up being action-packed. Queens outfielder Mo’ne Davis — who in 2014 became the first girl to pitch a winning game, throwing a shutout in the Little League World Series — made history once again by scoring the first run in the WPBL. She was driven in by Maggie Foxx, a pitcher-outfielder.
The first home run of the league was also scored during the opener. Heights catcher Denae Benites went long, cranking one to center.

title: John Leguizamo Reflects On Voicing Sid From ‘Ice Age,’ Says Role Covered Kids’ College Tuition
summary: John Leguizamo reflected on voicing Sid the sloth in the “Ice Age” franchise during a July 16 interview with Entertainment Tonight.
story: John Leguizamo has portrayed a diversity of characters, from hardened mechanic Aurelio in the “John Wick” franchise, to drag queen ingenue in “To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything!”
One particular role holds a unique place in Leguizamo’s career.

Leguizamo — who has been promoting the Christopher Nolan blockbuster hit “The Odyssey,” in which he plays blind swineherd Eumaeus — reflected on voicing Sid the sloth in the “Ice Age” franchise during a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight. The 66-year-old was candid about the life-changing role.
“It paid my bills. It got me a second and a triple home,” Leguizamo said. “It paid for my kids’ college.”

John Leguizamo — who shares two children with wife Justine Maurer, Allegra Sky Leguizamo and Ryder Lee Leguizamo — picked up the role more than 20 years ago for the first “Ice Age” movie that premiered in 2002. The franchise went on to make several sequels including 2006’s “The Meltdown” and 2009’s “Dawn of the Dinosaurs.”
Leguizamo told Entertainment Tonight that the films aren’t just financially rewarding. They’ve allowed him to show a bit more of his silly side.

“I can’t really let go of Sid the Sloth,” the actor said in the video, nearly slipping into the iconic voice. “It allowed me to be really as funny as I want to be. Movies are much more dramatic usually, but in that I got to be hilarious.”

The “Ice Age” era isn’t over yet. Another film, “Boiling Point,” is slated to come out in 2027 and will include not only Leguizamo but also several other returning faves including Denis Leary as Diego, Queen Latifah as Ellie and Ray Romano as Manny.

title: ‘Wonder Man’ Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Speaks Out Over Season 2 Cancellation After Show Was Renewed
summary: After reports circulated on July 30 that Marvel’s critically acclaimed show “Wonder Man” had been reportedly canceled, star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II took to social media to respond.
story: After reports circulated on July 30 that Marvel’s critically acclaimed show “Wonder Man” had been reportedly canceled, its star took to social media to respond.

Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, who plays main character Simon Williams, confirmed in a social media post that the show would not be returning after one season, saying, “that’s life, right?” The news comes just months after the show announced that it had been renewed for a second season.
The Marvel star thanked fans of the show, which debuted in January.

“Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back for Season 2. (And if you don’t knowww, now ya knoww! 😬)” Abdul-Mateen II, 40, wrote. “Everything will shake out. I wanted to say thank you to everybody who WATCHED the show, ENJOYED the show, and SHARED that they enjoyed the show in some way or other.”
Marvel did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.

The show, which ran for eight episodes, followed aspiring Hollywood actor Simon Williams as he attempts to make it in the entertainment industry. Along the way, he meets actor Trevor Slattery, played by Ben Kingsley, whose colorful past has placed him in a rather difficult spot in his career. After getting the chance to star in iconic director Von Kovak’s remake of superhero film “Wonder Man,” Simon grows closer to Trevor. And the two navigate the industry while also working through secrets of their own.

Abdul Mateen said plainly that the “show worked.” He also acknowledged the positive reception from fans and said that he had been following viewers’ reactions. As of Aug. 1, the show scores a 91% on Rotten Tomatoes.

“The show worked. And that’s my favorite thing about it,” he said. “I could see it on the faces of the Youtube Reactors (because I watched along with y’all this time. Shoutout to y’all) and I can see in the messages I get saying how the show reminded some of you not to give up, and I feel it in the genuine love shared when I bump into some of you all during the day.”
Abdul Mateen, whose performance in the Marvel show earned him an Emmy nomination for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series, said he was proud to be a “part of something cool.”
“Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the EMMYS. 🫡✌🏾” he wrote.

The news came as a shock to fans. In March, Marvel announced that the show would be returning for a second season. And during an April panel hosted by The Hollywood Reporter, several of those involved touched on what the then-upcoming season would look like. Writer Andrew Guest told the crowd that writing had already begun.
“Simon still has super powers. It is still about this relationship, about two artists, and our industry,” Guest said. “That is essentially what we want to maintain.”

title: Is A ‘New Girl’ Reunion In The Works? Max Greenfield Addresses Rumors on TODAY
summary: Max Greenfield shared some news on the rumors around a “New Girl” reunion while on TODAY.
story: Max Greenfield has found our flabbergast button. And guess what? He pressed it.

The actor stopped by TODAY on July 31 to chat about several of his upcoming projects. And while catching up with hosts Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones, Greenfield — who played the dramatic, image-obsessed yet endearing Schmidt on hit sitcom “New Girl” — dropped some big news.
“As far as I know, it’s happening,” Greenfield said of a “New Girl” reunion.
Greenfield, who’s currently promoting upcoming film “Don’t Say Good Luck,’ added that he’s “seen the scripts” for the sitcom.
“They’re amazing,” he said.
Showrunner Liz Meriwether shared a video on Aug. 1, responding to Greenfield’s comments on TODAY. She joked that “Max has just been very adamantly asking to be the ‘New Girl.’”
“He wants the title to be ‘Max Greenfield Is The New Girl,’” Meriwether said in the clip that was posted on Instagram.
Meriwether continued, saying that there’s been a “lot of back and forth about it.”
“I did think the scripts were amazing personally until they got, you know, sort of ripped apart,” she joked. “I wasn’t gonna say any of this publicly, but then Max decided to make it all public.”

“New Girl,” which aired on Fox, ran from 2011 to 2018. The show — which, in addition to Greenfield, starred Zooey Deschanel, Jake Johnson, Lamorne Morris, Hannah Simone and Damon Wayans Jr. – centered around quirky, awkward teacher Jess, played by Deschanel, after she moves into a Los Angeles loft with three guys she found on Craigslist.
While Greenfield visited TODAY, Jenna and Sheinelle played some clips of his fellow “New Girl” cast mates, discussing the possibility of a reunion.

In one clip, comedian Lamorne Morris, who played Winston Bishop in the sitcom, tells TODAY during a May visit that he wanted to do a reunion “because I love the fans so much.” However, he jokes, that co-star Johnson, who played Nick Miller, had no interest in doing so.
In another video, Johnson jokingly accuses Morris of being the issue while on TODAY in July.

“Lamorne said, ‘All jokes aside, I don’t respect anybody at the TODAY Show. I don’t respect what they do. I don’t respect fans. I don’t respect humans because I am greater than,’” Johnson said, prompting laughs from hosts Al Roker and Dylan Dreyer.
YOUTHS! Amirite?
Well, Greenfield responded to the clips with a pretty Schmidt-like statement.
“I mean, obviously, you can see these are morons,” he joked. “I’m not gonna play the game.”
The actor also told Jenna and Sheinelle that Meriwether had been worried that wasn’t sure if there were “any more stories to tell.”
“She’s full of them,” Greenfield said.

In her response video, Meriwether joked that she had been quite proud of her scripts, but the cast had far too many notes. She joked that Johnson requested that his character be “really thin and wants to be naked a lot, showing off his body.”

“He asked to have a dance number with him fully nude, dancing to ‘Levitating’ by Dua Lipa,” Meriwether said in the video. “It didn’t really make any sense in the story, so I kind of tried to figure out a way to tell him I didn’t want that. He got really upset.”
She also went on to claim that Morris wanted his character to wear copious amounts of jewelry.

“He wants a very long chain, like a chain all the way down to his knees. Again, it kind of didn’t make a ton of sense for the character and the story,” Meriwether said. “And I mean, we could do it. That one felt sort of doable, but I thought it would maybe kind of throw audiences.”
Winnie with a ridiculous chain? Hey, we’re not against it.

The show, which ended after seven seasons, received critical acclaim, earning five Emmy nominations and five Golden Globe nominations as well. While the sitcom was highly successful during its run, it later on drew renewed interest on streaming services as many turned to the show as a comfort watch amid the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: What Happens in the ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ End Credits Scene?
summary: Find out what Marvel confirmed about Tom Holland’s future in the MCU in the ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day” end credits scene.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” below.

Superheroes of past and present will come together when “Avengers: Doomsday” is released in December. But there has been one noticeable absence from the list of many heroes who are set to appear: Spider-Man.

Although Tom Holland’s Peter Parker/Spider-Man previously starred in 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame,” Marvel has not revealed what role, if any, he’ll play in the next team up. But at the end of the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” fans received a hint as to where Spider-Man’s story is headed next.

The new MCU flick, released July 31, shows Spider-Man dealing with the aftermath of Doctor Strange’s spell in 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home” that caused everyone to forget him. Now, he has to learn who he is, both as Peter and his hero alter ego, while finding the identity of a mysterious being who can control psyches.

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” also stars Zendaya as MJ, Jacob Batalon as Ned, Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle/Punisher, Florence Pugh as Yelena/Black Widow, Tramell Tillman as William “Bill” Metzger, Mark Ruffalo as Bruce Banner/Hulk and Sadie Sink, whose secret role is revealed about halfway through the film.

Initially, the web-slinger believes he knows the enemy he is fighting against, but he later discovers he has been lied to. The final act puts Spider-Man in a precarious situation, where he sustains a serious injury.
Does he survive? And does Marvel confirm when fans will see him again? Find out below.
What Happens at the End of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’?
For the first half of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” our hero is searching for an unknown villain, played by Sink, who is trying to gain access to the Department of Damage Control building.

Sink keeps herself hidden by using her telepathic abilities to borrow the identities of multiple strangers. But when Spider-Man finally catches a glimpse of her, he runs her image through facial recognition software and confirms her name: Jean Grey.

The audience, and Spider-Man, learn that Jean is wreaking havoc because she wants to find her sister Sara, who was kidnapped by DODC head Metzger for having telepathic powers. While in captivity, Jean realizes that Metzger performed tests on Sara, killing her. He plans to use the same experiment on Jean.

Spider-Man rushes to rescue a captured Jean and stop her from killing Metzger. He defeats a group of Hand ninjas controlled by Jean and arrives just in time to have a heart-to-heart with her. He explains that he has also felt the pain of losing someone close to him, and they form a friendship. Seconds later, Punisher accidentally shoots Spider-Man.
He survives the nearly fatal wound thanks to Jean’s powers. While he heals and returns to protecting the citizens of New York City, Jean leaves town.
Will Spider-Man Appear in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’?

In the final scene of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” Peter enters a bodega and spots Ned. He decides he no longer wants to face the world alone and goes to introduce himself. Peter and Ned perform their secret handshake, breaking the spell and unlocking Ned’s past memories of Peter.
The film ends and the credits roll. But as Marvel fans know, a MCU movie is never truly over until after the end credits scene.
The one shown in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is short, but still includes a clue about where Spider-Man will be seen next.

In the post-credits scene, the screen of Ned’s “Spidey Tracker” app is shown. However, the app is unable to locate Spider-Man on Earth. The app searches for the web-slinger in the galaxy and determines he is somewhere in space.
“Spider-Man will return,” text on the screen reads, not confirming when that will be or if fans should expect him to pop up in “Avengers: Doomsday.”
But, the scene does confirm that Holland will suit up again.

title: Jason Kelce Shares His Favorite Moments From Travis and Taylor Swift’s Wedding
summary: Jason Kelce is revealing major details about Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s star-studded wedding, from the wide-range of attendees to emotional moments.
story: Jason Kelce is revealing major details about Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s star-studded wedding, from the wide-range of attendees to emotional moments.

The retired NFL player, who served as his younger brother’s best man at the July 3 nuptials, visited Philadelphia radio station 94WIP and spoke about the Madison Square Garden event in a clip posted on Instagram July 30.
When asked about the ceremony, Jason Kelce described it as “incredible” and “more than 10 out of 10.”
He also shared that he became emotional as he watched Swift and his brother celebrate their love story.
“I am a crier. I did cry ... Probably cried more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding, which probably is not acceptable,” he joked.
Jason Kelce playfully added that his wife Kylie Kelce was “probably not happy about that.”
He confirmed that Adam Sandler officiated the ceremony, praising the comedian for being the ideal person for the job.

“Obviously, he’s hilarious and he knows how to make it entertaining and funny, but there’s a sweetness to Adam in everything he does, all of his movies, that really resonated throughout,” Jason Kelce explained.
Speaking about the bride and groom, he continued, “I think that Taylor and Travis were fantastic in the ceremony.”
He revealed that the pair strayed from a traditional reception and instead threw a giant party with their friends and family.

“My favorite moments were just the different people that are at this wedding, right? Like, in one moment, I’m going (from) seeing Brad Pitt pop out of a corner and talking to him, and then in the next moment, I’m seeing Mrs. Clark who ran the attendance at Cleveland Heights High School,” he shared.

Jason Kelce took some time to catch up with his former teacher and reminisce about his younger days when he tried to mimic his dad’s voice to call out sick. Other friends and relatives from their hometown were there, he said, as well as more famous faces like Conan O’Brien.
“It was an amazing evening with a lot of awesome people, and, you know, just so happy for both Travis and Taylor,” he said.
In another clip, Jason Kelce expressed how surprised he is that pictures from the wedding still haven’t leaked.

“I haven’t seen any legitimate photos really from the wedding. It’s remarkable that there was a thousand people inside Madison Square Garden ... and there’s really not a lot out there,” he pointed out.
He also said that the lack of pictures shows how much effort his brother and sister-in-law put in to make their special day feel “intimate.”
He noted the “backlash” the two received for holding their wedding at the New York City arena and said that the space “didn’t feel like Madison Square (Garden).”

“They did a great job of finding an area that could be very secure,” he continued. “Some place that they would be able to have this kind of control over it, while also feeling intimate and really special. It was incredibly done.”
In the weeks since the nuptials, more information about the pop icon and the Kansas City Chiefs star’s unique venue and ceremony have emerged — mostly thanks to Jason Kelce.
He previously told the Reno Gazette Journal that all four of his daughters — Wyatt, 6, Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 1 — were flower girls.
“They’re beautiful, they’re incredible personalities,” the proud dad gushed about his daughters. “And Travis and Taylor love them.”

title: Who Is Sadie Sink’s Character in ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’?
summary: Following months of seeing Sadie Sink cloaked in shadows in trailers, fans learned her character’s identity in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Find out who she is playing.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” below.

Following months of seeing Sadie Sink cloaked in shadows in trailers and hearing her remain tight-lipped whenever pressed about her role in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” her character and her possible influence in the future of the Marvel Cinematic Universe have been revealed.

The latest MCU entry, out July 31, is the fourth installment in Tom Holland’s Spider-Man era, introducing a more mature tone as Peter Parker grapples with his identity and being alone in the world after losing his aunt May (Marisa Tomei) and his friends. Holland returns as the titular character, with Zendaya as MJ, Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle/Punisher and Sink as …
While fans have known that Sink will appear in the superhero flick for over a year, the identity of her character and the major villain have been kept a secret.
The trailers showed glimpses of Sink’s character in a hood, seemingly watching Spider-Man tackle a threat that has the ability to take control of any psyche, with the exception of the web-slinger.

Given Sink’s distinctive red hair and the return of the early 2000s X-Men characters in “Avengers: Doomsday,” it has been speculated that the “Stranger Things” alum will take on the role of Jean Grey. The powerful mutant, with powers of telekinesis, telepathy and pyrokinesis, was previously portrayed by Famke Janssen and Sophie Turner.

So, were the rumors true and the Phoenix has made her grand debut in the MCU? Or has Marvel been hiding a twist? Read on to find out who Sink plays in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and what happens to her character.
Sadie Sink’s ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Character Revealed

In the film’s first act, Spider-Man tracks down a military tank that is speeding through New York City. The tank crashes into a prison holding a villain he captured in an opening montage named Scorpion (Michael Mando).

When Spider-Man opens the tank, he finds a confused woman who doesn’t remember how she ended up there. Spider-Man realizes that the woman is being mind controlled and she’s not the only one. An unknown mastermind begins to jump from person to person, taking over their minds and toying with Spider-Man.

Later when our hero encounters the Scorpion again, fans see that Sink’s character is the source of the telepathic abilities. She communicates with Spider-Man through Scorpion and warns him to stay out of her way unless he wants MJ to be put in danger. She also reveals that she wants information about “V-Max.”

Determined to track her down, Peter uses facial recognition software to learn where else the mysterious woman has been spotted before terrorizing New York. He teams up with MJ and reveals that while details about the woman’s life mostly lead to dead ends, he does find her name: Jean Grey.
Yes, the rumors were true. The role of Jean Grey has been passed to Sink and a new era of X-Men has arrived in the MCU.
But this Jean Grey is just learning the extent of her powers and can only inhabit beings that are about 33 feet away from her, which Spider-Man uses to his advantage.
Is Sadie Sink’s Character the Villain?

Spider-Man heads to the Department of Damage Control to stop Jean from breaking into a vault where department head William “Bill” Metzger (Tramell Tillman) is hiding with other employees. Despite Jean using her powers to briefly control Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) and Punisher, who arrives to assist Spider-Man, the masked hero outsmarts her and helps capture her.
Before Jean is taken away, she utters the name Sara to Spider-Man.

Fans then see a flashback scene from Jean’s perspective that reveals her backstory. Jean had an older sister named Sara who possessed the same powers. One day when the sisters were sitting in a park together practicing their skills, Sara went to get ice cream and never returned. She was taken by Metzger and his team. Despite being miles away, Sara communicated with Jean while in captivity, sending her one phrase: “V-Max.”

With the help of Florence Pugh’s Yelena/Black Widow (whose cameo in the film was hinted at by Marvel head Kevin Feige a few weeks ago), Spider-Man learns about Sara and realizes the telepath is not a maniacal villain but simply a woman trying to reunite with her sister.

He rushes to free Jean, who is being experimented on by Metzger in the same room where her sister was held. Jean looks at the ceiling and finds the answer she has been searching for. “V-Max” is the name of the company on the air vent above the holding cell, the last image Sara saw before she died.
What Happens to Sadie Sink’s Character at the End?
Spider-Man stops Jean, whose abilities become heightened in the cell, from killing Metzger and harming New Yorkers. They bond over their grief of losing a loved one and agree to be friends.
But during the heartfelt moment, Punisher accidentally shoots and wounds Spider-Man. Jean uses her powers to keep him alive until he wakes up on his own.
Jean’s final scene shows her leaving New York City. Her destination is unknown, meaning fans will have to wait and see if she reappears in “Avengers: Doomsday.”

title: Drew Starkey Shares His Reaction to His ‘Lucky’ Character’s Fate
summary: Drew Starkey shares his reaction to Cary’s death in Lucky and reveals behind-the-scenes details about the car chase scene from Episode 4.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
Warning: This contains spoilers for Episode 4 of “Lucky”

Fans of crime thriller “Lucky” were in for a surprise when Episode 4 aired on July 29 and Drew Starkey’s Cary Masterson, husband of titular character Lucky Armstrong (Anya Taylor-Joy), met a shocking fate.

Apple TV’s new limited series centers on con artist Lucky as she’s forced on the run after a multi-million dollar heist collapses. In the latest episode, Lucky finally tracks down her fellow con husband Cary after he abandoned her and took off with their stolen cash.

The couple shares an intense reunion, fueled by equally visceral anger and chemistry. But just as tensions are at their peak, they are forced to become partners-in-crime again when Cary’s house is busted by the FBI, and the two are surrounded.

After tossing his wife keys to the getaway car, Cary and Lucky kick off an adrenaline-pumping pursuit to escape the authorities. While they successfully get them off their tail several times, they just can’t make a clean break.

Desperate to deter the swarm, Cary starts shooting at the tires of the police car behind them, which leads to one officer firing back. One of his bullets strikes a tire on Cary and Lucky’s car, causing their vehicle to flip multiple times.

When Lucky wakes up after impact, she sees that Cary survived the crash but was struck by a bullet. Although she desperately tries to stop the bleeding and save his life, her efforts just aren’t enough.
“You were happy...” Cary slurs to his wife in his final moments alive.
Below, Starkey breaks down the character, his fate and more for TODAY.com.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.
What a full circle moment for a tragic character. There’s so much love that me and Anya try to imbue into the characters, and it’s kind of a fitting way for it to end. But obviously it’s sad.
I think it adds an element of surprise, and I think it also adds an extra layer of motivation for Lucky. She’s been through a lot, and this is just one more notch that she has to work through.

One: The mystery around the character, and the challenge of trying to convince someone in front of me that I love, that what I did wasn’t wrong, and that I had the right intentions. Also, the team involved. Our showrunners and Anya, that was just the perfect cocktail.

Oh my gosh, incredible. The car chase sequence — it took about a week of filming in Long Beach, and it’s always interesting because you shoot it in such little parts. So yeah, kudos to our editors. They really crafted something beautiful.

I think the montage sequence of them in Las Vegas celebrating. I mean, you really could see Cary and Lucky in their true form together, just free. It really feels like two young kids enjoying themselves, which was a lot of fun. We were shooting in Vegas with real people in the casinos, and it was a blast.

There were plenty of memorable moments, but in between takes, or if I had a little break, I remember I would walk off to the blackjack tables and play a couple rounds of blackjack and lose my money, and then jump back to set, kind of dejected. Our director Jonathan Van Tulleken would be like, “You good?” I’m like, “Ah, I’m fine. It’s nothing. I’m going to go back and win my money back at some point.”

I think just because they’re complicated, and there’s something about the characters on the first read on the page that I don’t quite get and understand, I think that’s always a good sign. You want to keep asking questions about these characters. Just the challenge of it I think is fun, and the contradiction.

title: WNBA Star Brittney Griner Files For Divorce, Citing ‘Irretrievably Broken’ Marriage
summary: WNBA star Brittney Griner has filed for divorce from her wife Cherelle Griner, according to court documents filed on July 30.
story: WNBA star Brittney Griner has filed for divorce from her wife Cherelle Griner, according to court documents filed on July 30.
Brittney Griner, who legally married her wife in June 2018, said in the divorce petition that the marriage is “irretrievably broken” and that there is “no hope of reconciliation.”
Griner is seeking joint custody of their son, Bash Raymond, according to the petition, which was filed in Fulton County Superior Court in Georgia.
The Connecticut Sun star has been separated from her wife, an attorney, since July 24, according to the divorce petition.
As recently as July 27, the athlete had been sharing glimpses of the couple’s home life, including a YouTube video of the pair and their young son making short ribs.

The couple’s relationship was made particularly public amid the athlete’s 10-month detainment in Russia. The basketball star, who had played for Russian team UMMC Ekaterinburg, was arrested in the country on drug charges in 2022 after officials said that they found vape cartridges containing oil derived from cannabis in her luggage. Griner’s defense, however, argued that she used the substance to treat her injuries.

During the monthslong fight for the WNBA star’s freedom, Cherelle Griner became a vocal advocate for her wife. She helped mobilize fans, the league, along with politicians to speak out on behalf of the detained player.
“Your prayers and support are greatly appreciated,” Cherelle Griner wrote on Instagram. I love my wife wholeheartedly, so this message comes during one of the weakest moments of my life.”
This is the WNBA star’s second marriage. She was briefly married to fellow basketball player Glory Johnson in 2015. They share two children, Ava Simone and Solei Diem.

title: Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Reviews: Why Critics Say It’s Her ‘Most Musically Accomplished’ Album
summary: What are critics saying about Ariana Grande’s album Petal” Read reviews for Ariana Grande’s album Petal.
story: “Petal,” Ariana Grande’s eighth studio album, is here and the singer is hoping her fans will connect with the album’s unique vibe.

“I think they’ll feel familiarity and comfort in it because it just feels like it pulls from many different parts of myself. And yet at the same time, it is very experimental and different for me,” she said in an interview with Apple Music.
While chatting about her new album, “Petal,” the 33-year-old described her writing process, saying she “wrote from a place that I don’t usually.”
Grande said she tapped into the “unfiltered rage that I think we all feel sometimes.”
“I usually am too shy to tap into that, and I think this time I kind of just didn’t filter as much as I usually do,” she said.
What are critics saying about “Petal” after listening to the entire album? Here are some of the initial reviews.
The New York Times

The New York Times suggests that Grande sounds “irritated with the invasive nature of fame” throughout “Petal,” which the publication says “trades her signature effervescence for something darker and more brooding.”
The New York Times describes the timing of this album as “a bit odd.”

“For one thing, it comes less than two years after Grande revealed that she was planning to put more of her creative energy into comedic acting and musical theater rather than pop stardom,” the review reads.
The publication also highlights the fact that the album is being released in the middle of Grande’s tour to promote her previous album, “Eternal Sunshine.”

“That urgency suggests ‘Petal’ is the sort of album a musician makes when she has something new or important to express, but these 12 tracks are disappointingly light on revelation,” the review reads.
The New York Times describes “Eternal Sunshine” as “a work of sharp craftsmanship and tonal variety.” In comparison, the publication says “Petal” “feels murky and monochrome in comparison.”

“As usual, Grande’s vocals are lovely and impressively arranged; she can still sing circles, squares and curlicues around most A-list pop stars. But the material here is mostly a morass of sluggish tempos that lacks the charisma and conviction of her best work,” the review reads.
The Associated Press
The Associated Press says Grande shows “real restraint” on “Petal,” a vibe that was foreshadowed by the lead single, “Hate That I Made You Love Me.”
“There is a variety of textures here, and they are cooler than ever before — nearing lackadaisical, but still retaining a lot of charm,” the review reads.
The publication says “Petal” lacks Grande’s “signature runs” and “larger-than-life” vocal moments.
“Grande has moved on, as she is entitled to do. But is her ‘Big Feelings’ subtlety enough to keep loyalists engaged?” the review reads.
The publication’s review ends with a reflection on the overall vibe of the album.

“In the press materials for ‘Petal,’ Grande described the album as ‘Something that is full of life and growing through the cracks of something cold and hard and challenging.’ There is some truth to it: Across these dozen songs are small joys, buried beneath atmospheric production and listless melodies. But there is also a freedom to pop’s most elastic vocalist choosing to rein it in,” it reads.
Pitchfork
Giving the album a 6.5 out of 10, Pitchfork says “Petal” has an “intimate, experimental feel” and features “songwriting that often lacks the urgency and precision of her best.”
“But on the whole, rather than a dramatic departure, ‘Petal’ feels fairly constrained and, occasionally, like a tame reimagining of her older work,” the review reads.
Pitchfork argues that the album’s “strongest moments come when Grande ventures into less familiar territory.”

“The soft shuffle of speed garage provides a sublime counterpoint to her celestial harmonies on ‘oh well’; jangling, sun-bleached indie-pop brings an Olivia Rodrigo-esque feel to ‘bad thing (bunny hop).’ On ‘stay,’ assisted by Max Martin, she comes closest to the breezy frankness of her career high, ‘thank u, next,’ with ‘Petal’s’  most full-chested vocal performance and bare-hearted lyrics,” the review reads.
Variety

Compared to Grande’s 2024 album, “Eternal Sunshine,” Variety says “Petal” is “darker, moodier and a lot more blunt.” The publication describes the singer’s emotions in “Petal” as “more volatile, less heartbroken, and much less internalized.”
Variety notes that Grande’s innuendos move “into a whole new realm” with plenty of NSFW lyrics throughout the album.

“The heartbroken but resilient Grande from the last album is nowhere in sight — with one exception, these songs are about vengeance or sex, and about whom is bound to be the subject of endless online chatter,” the publication writes.
“Kiss Me” and “Freak” are two examples of “familiar-sounding songs and moments,” per Variety, but the album is also full of music that “would be more expected from FKA Twigs or even the Weeknd.”
Variety called the closing ballad, “Nowhere, Nobody,” the “prettiest song” on the album.
Overall, the publication described “Petal” as “the biggest musical departure of her career” and “her most musically and lyrically accomplished album.”
Rolling Stone

Grande wrote “Petal” from a place of rage and Rolling Stone says it “suits her musically.” The publication says “Hate That I Made You Love Me” “serves as a thematic warning for the mood Ari’s in these days.”
Rolling Stone notes that Grande “rages against the tabloid rumor mill” in her new album.
“The songs on ‘Petal’ are mostly moody midtempo electro-chill, brooding rather than banging,” the review reads, calling “Freak” the “most clever” song.
Compared to “Eternal Sunshine,” which Rolling Stone describes as “ornate and meticulously crafted,” “Petal” is “much more loose and spontaneous.”
“She’s shooting from the hip, both musically and emotionally,” the review reads.
The publication says Grande’s “f--- it attitude” is “loud and clear” on “Petal.” In short, “that attitude brings out Ariana Grande at her best.”
Billboard

Billboard says “Petal” finds Grande “shape-shifting into a darker, more guitar-driven sound that builds on the ethereal glimmer of 2024’s ‘Eternal Sunshine’ and its 2025 ‘Brighter Days Ahead’ deluxe tracks.”
The publication describes “Petal” as a “manicured middle finger aimed directly at the public.”

“’Petal’ finds Grande not just directly addressing the precarious relationship between her celebrity and person — as she so deftly does on the excellent title track — but also celebrating the first signs of new life born out of particularly volatile periods like 2025. Some of that new life (petals in the pavement, if you will) looks like a rejuvenated perspective on privacy, maturation and the beautiful unknown of the path not chosen (’Freak’), and other parts of that new life are anchored by a sense of self that’s stronger than ever because it embraces and cherishes all of its past iterations (’Never Get Over Me’),” the review reads.

If you loved “Dangerous Woman” and “Thank U, Next,” Billboard says you’ll “feel right at home” with “Petal” since it “effortlessly balances straightforward pop bangers (’Stay’) with quippy, candid songwriting (’Oh Well’).”

“Where earlier albums had moments that felt as though Grande was acting out a caricature of her pop persona; ‘Petal’ seems to emerge from somewhere much more grounded, which allows Grande to sneak in meaningful personal revelations in between genuinely hilarious digs,” the review reads.
Billboard says the lyrics are “at times, underdeveloped” but says the album was “clearly crafted to be performed live — perhaps more so than any of her previous LPs.”

title: Why Is the Internet Obsessed with a 500-Page, 24-Year-Old Book About Salt?
summary: Why is “Salt” going viral? Mark Kulansky responds to his book Salt going viral after Wyatt Derman’s video about it.
story: Hockey romances with steamy turns, thrillers packed with suspense, self-help books with life-changing promises … and around 500 pages on a mineral.
Mark Kurlansky’s bestseller “Salt: A World History” stands out among the internet’s current favorite books.

Published in 2002, the nonfiction text studies how salt has shaped civilization — from serving as a currency, to provoking wars, to becoming an ordinary but essential item on kitchen tables around the world.
The book’s recent viral moment is largely thanks to an Instagram reel from creator Wyatt Derman that has garnered over 780,000 likes.

In his now-viral post, Derman explained how “Salt” changed how he perceives the world around him: “I’ve become a man who can’t pass a salt shaker without feeling the weight of human civilization … turns out nothing’s actually boring,” he said in part.
Kurlansky tells TODAY.com that his 26-year-old daughter was the first to spot the trend online and alert him about it.
“It’s in the nature of going viral, you hear about it instantly,” Kurlansky says.
Since then, the online success has prompted Kurlansky to start his first Instagram account. Through the platform, Derman reached out to the author, and the two are now planning a live Q&A together.
Kurlansky says Derman’s reaction to the book was “exactly” what he had hoped for when he wrote the book.

Derman, speaking to TODAY.com, says he first picked up the book while on the hunt for a read that would “invigorate” his curiosity. Avoiding self-help picks, he skipped over to the bookstore’s world and food sections. There, he found Kurlansky’s book.
“I was curious, what in the world could make somebody go and spend great lengths of time to write about salt, and why would they do that?” he says. So, he decided to find out for himself.
Although Derman says he wasn’t expecting much when he first opened “Salt,” he quickly found himself sharing what he learned with family members.

Months later, he decided to bring some of those discoveries to Instagram in his now-viral reel — like how the words “salary” and “salad” derive from salt. Some of the anecdotes stuck with other Instagram users, per his comments.
“Just wanted to let you know I’ve thought about this at least once a day for the last 10 days,” one user wrote.

Other users have posted reels about “Salt” in recent weeks, too. “So, are we all collectively reading a 500 page book about salt now or...” one user wrote in a video that has garnered over 90,000 likes.
Although Kurlansky liked Derman’s video, he pushed back on one small point the creator alluded to: exploring pepper next.
“I don’t look for commodities to write about, I look for great stories,” the author explains. “Pepper isn’t nearly as good a story as salt.”
Kurlansky has published other books on commodities, though, including bestseller “Cod: A Biography of a Fish That Changed the World,” which predated “Salt.”
Ultimately, writing about ordinary commodities isn’t where he derives his success, he says — storytelling is.
“Nothing is boring if you tell it in a good story,” Kurlansky says. “A good story is never boring.”

And to that point, Derman agrees: “A good story is what makes the world go ‘round,” he says. But, he adds: “From what I read about pepper, I think there’s a good story there. I wouldn’t be opposed to him writing a book on pepper.”

title: Steven Spielberg Predicted the Superhero Boom Back on TODAY in 1982
summary: Steven Spielberg and comic book legend Jack Kirby spoke to TODAY in 1982 about why comic book characters are perfect for movies.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment, highlighting the growth of movies based on comic books, is from June 11, 1982.

Films based on comic books go together like popcorn and coming attractions. It’s a combination that seems made for each other, and one that TODAY spotlighted back in 1982, an era when comic book characters like Superman, Popeye and Little Orphan Annie graced the silver screen.

And while Popeye and Annie are hardly superheroes like we’ve come to know in recent years, they did spring from the pages of comic books and provided fans entertainment with their escapades. The comic book superhero movie movement shows no signs of slowing down and will keep going when “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” starring Tom Holland, slings into theaters on July 31.
What Did TODAY Say About Comic Book Superheroes in the Movies in 1982?
“Comic book heroes have been showing up on movie screens pretty regularly of late,” former TODAY co-host Jane Pauley said as she introduced the segment.
“It’s a trend that is likely to continue,” she added.

That was an understatement. We live in a golden era of comic book adaptations, but in 1982 the trend was really just getting underway. Comic book movies, from “Batman” and “Superman” to “Black Widow” and “Captain America,” are as much a staple of films today as end credit scenes.
“It’s not surprising that the movies, since their inception, have robbed the comic books of their heroes,” NBC’s Jim Brown said in his story.
“Few characters in literature have endured as well as the fantasy figures from pulp literature,” he added. “And nothing seems to diminish the popularity of comic books and comic book heroes.”
Comic Book Veteran Jack Kirby on the Need for Heroes

The late Jack Kirby, a legend in the comic book field known for creating or co-creating iconic characters and franchises like Hulk, Captain America, the Fantastic Four, Avengers and X-Men, felt audiences longed for superheroes.
“We’ve always needed them. We’ve always had them,” Kirby said.
“That’s good for us. I think it balances life. It gives us a kind of balance we need. If we had reality all the time, I don’t think we could take it,” he added.
Steven Spielberg Sensed the Value in Bringing Comic Book Characters to the Big Screen

Legendary director Steven Spielberg had a watershed year in 1982, with the releases of his non-comic book associated films “E.T.” and “Poltergeist.” Still, he understood why comic book heroes appealed to moviegoers.
“More things happen to heroes in one two-hour movie than happens to 100,000 people in all of their combined lifetimes,” he said.

“And that’s just the state of the art in the motion picture business, that you’re able to take all those frustrations ... you take all those fantasies and you put them all together in a big melting pot and you say, ‘This is my view of the world’ and ‘These are my fantasies I’ve always had about what I’ve wanted to become’ — now you be that person.”
The Idea That Comic Books Could Lead to Big Bucks at the Box Office Was Blossoming
Movies based on comic books are big business today. In 1982, Kirby could see what was on the horizon.

“The creative people are on a certain plane, and the publisher is on a certain plane. He lives with his lawyers and accountants, and he says, ‘Well, let’s get toys out of this. Let’s get films out of this. Let’s get sweaters out of this.’ And he’s only adhering to a commercial generation,” he said.

title: Read the Letter George Clooney Wrote To His Town’s Mayor After Evacuating Wildfires in France
summary: George Clooney sent a letter to the mayor Didier Bremond of Brignoles, France after he and wife Amal Clooney fled their home there due to wildfires in the region.
story: George and Amal Clooney were forced to flee their home in southeastern France this week amid wildfires in the region. The actor sent a heartfelt message to their town’s mayor, pledging his continued commitment to the community.
Clooney’s letter to Didier Bremond, the mayor of Brignoles, the town of 18,000 he’s called home since 2021, was shared in Reuters by the actor’s publicist.

“Dear Didier. At this point we have no idea whether our beautiful home makes it through this terrible moment and as we evacuate Brignoles we want to emphasize two things,” the actor wrote in the letter. “First, we hope you and the people of our city are safe.”
Clooney added that secondly, “Amal and I are committed to making sure that whatever happens to our village, we are part of this community and we’ll be part of making it whole.”
“We love Brignoles and our friends who live there,” the actor wrote.

As of July 31, France’s Var area, which includes Brignoles, has experienced a fire flare-up west of the town of Correns, according to the region’s website. There are evacuation orders in place for parts of the town, which is a roughly 20-minute drive from Brignoles.

Local authorities said that the fires on Wednesday burned through an estimated 100 hectares of land, which comes out to 250 acres. Roughly 700 residents who evacuated the area were permitted to return to their homes.

Last year, the high-profile couple and their twins Ella and Alexander obtained French citizenship. In a 2025 interview with Esquire, George Clooney said that the couple decided to raise their children abroad, so that the twins could live a quieter life.

“You know, we live on a farm in France. A good portion of my life growing up was on a farm, and as a kid I hated the whole idea of it,” Clooney said. “But now, for them, it’s like — they’re not on their iPads, you know? They have dinner with grown-ups and have to take their dishes in. They have a much better life.”
Clooney acknowledged that he had been “worried” about raising his children in the “culture of Hollywood,” had the family stayed in Los Angeles.

“I felt like they were never going to get a fair shake at life. France — they kind of don’t give a s--- about fame,” he told Esquire. “I don’t want them to be walking around worried about paparazzi. I don’t want them being compared to somebody else’s famous kids.”

title: This Is What Barack Obama Read and Listened to This Summer — And People Have Thoughts
summary: It’s that time of the year when Barack Obama shares his summer playlist and reading list.
story: It’s that time of the year when Barack Obama shares his summer playlist and reading list.
The former president is known for sharing the books and songs that he has enjoyed over the sunny months, always surprising people with his selections and asking for recommendations.
This year is no different as Obama posted 11 books that captured his attention these past months, as well as a slew of songs that he couldn’t get enough of.

Among the novels that he read include “Kin” by Tayari Jones about two daughters raised without mothers in Honeysuckle, Louisiana. There’s also Ann Patchett’s “Whistler” about a woman who reunites with her stepfather who she hasn’t seen in 40 years. Obama also read Colson Whitehead’s final volume in his “Harlem Trilogy,” “Cool Machine.” The author recently sat down with Craig Melvin for his “Glass Half Full” podcast to discuss the novel.
And when it came to his music selection, Obama treated his social media followers to plenty of hits.

“Here are some of the songs I’ve been listening to this summer,” the former politician captioned his list. “It starts with a song Michelle and I love by Glen Hansard, a great musician who passed tragically this week. Our hearts go out to his family.”

Obama’s taste in music is wide ranging from R&B and rap with “Girl, Get Up” by Doechii and SZA, to rock with “Going Shopping” by The Strokes” to Latin music with Rawayana and Manuel Turizo’s “Inglés en Miami.”
Obama also enjoys classics like Earth, Wind and Fire’s “Can’t Hide Love,” “Modern Love” by David Bowie and “Let’s Get It On” by Marvin Gaye.
Like most years, people paid particular attention to one or two tracks that made it on Obama’s playlist. Many were surprised (and loved) to see “Motion Party” by BossMan Dlow.

“The thought of Obama singing ‘this a motion party you cannot get iiinnnn’ 😭😭😭😭😭,” one person commented, while another added, “Motion Party being on this list is one of the reasons why you’ll always be my President!! 😭😂.”
Even BossMan himself was surprised, commenting, “It’s A Motion Party We Gotta Let Obama Innn.”

Other artists that were included in his playlist also thanked him, including Sheryl Crow who wrote, “Man, I’m super honored that someone I admire so much is listening to a deep deep cut from my second record. Very cool, @barackobama!”
Fred Hammond commented, “Heeeeyyy thank you sir. Truly an honor,” while Anderson .Paak added, “That’s my dog!”
In the comment section of his post, Obama also asked people for suggestions.
“I’m always looking for new songs to listen to, so please share any recommendations in the comments,” he wrote.

title: Karol G Asked a Little Girl What Her Favorite Song Was. The Answer Made the Entire Stadium Laugh
summary: When Karol G asked a young fan at her concert what her favorite song was, she replied that it was “Dai Dai” by Shakira.
story: It was a night to remember for Karol G and one young fan who made the whole stadium smile at the singer’s latest show.

During her July 29 “Viajando Por El Mundo TropiTour” concert at Rogers Stadium in Toronto, Karol took a moment to say hi to a little girl in the crowd. In video shared by DJ Mechon on Instagram, Karol stopped the music, gave the girl a hug and asked her name.
“Chloe,” she replied, before Karol asked what her favorite song was. “Dai Dai,” the girl replied, referring to Shakira’s song for the World Cup.
“What?” Karol replied, before realizing she was not talking about one of her songs. “’Dai Dai,’ let’s sing it,” she said in Spanish. “She knows it.”
“She just said that her favorite song is ‘Dai Dai’ by Shakira,” Karol continued as the audience laughed. “You want to sing it? You know it?”
The girl then started to sing Shakira’s song, with everyone joining in and Karol cheering her on.

“This was one of the most special moments of the night because it showed both the innocence of children and Karol G’s kindness,” DJ Mechon, who attended the concert and recorded the video, tells TODAY.com. “When she asked the little girl what her favorite song was, she answered ‘Dai Dai,’ which is actually a Shakira song. Rather than making the child feel embarrassed, Karol G embraced the moment, and as the little girl sang, the entire stadium joined in.”

Adding, “It turned into one of the most genuine and heartwarming moments of the concert,” he continued, adding that “being there, for what was probably the biggest Latin concert  Toronto has ever seen, was unforgettable. The energy, emotion, and connection between Karol G and her fans made it a truly special night.”
Julie Haynes, another fan who attended the same concert and shared video of the moment online, also tells TODAY.com that the interaction was among her favorites of the night.

“Out of the whole concert, that was the moment that stuck with me the most. It was so innocent and genuine,” Haynes says. “I love how kids are just unapologetically themselves, and seeing her confidently tell Karol G that her favorite song was ‘Dai Dai’ by Shakira was such a sweet moment I’ll never forget.”
And it was a memorable night for Karol as she became the first female solo artist to headline a show at Rogers Stadium.

The “Latina Foreva” singer kicked off her “Viajando Por El Mundo TropiTour” on July 27 in Chicago, with fans calling the show a celebration of culture, fawning over her sensational outfits and band on stage.
Just in the past days while on tour, Karol announced her new single, “Matadora,” as well as a new album “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto.”

During her Toronto concert, she revealed that it will be released on Friday, Aug. 7. The cover art was also unveiled on the screens. She will continue touring across North America, Latin America and Europe, marking her largest live production yet.

title: Are ‘Love Island USA’s’ Aniya And Carl Together? Here’s What They Told Andy Cohen About
summary: Are ‘Love Island USA’s’ Aniya and Carl together after the finale? Are they dating? They just gave a relationship update. Here’s where they stand now.
story: It’s been a few weeks since the “Love Island USA” Season 8 finale aired, and fans are dying to know one question about their faves Aniya Harvey and Carl Schmidt: Are they together or not?
Well, the pair finally has an answer for us.

During a July 29 appearance on Bravo’s late night talk show “Watch What Happens Live,” Aniya and Carl, who were featured alongside the competition winners Trinity Tatum and Bryce Alakai, gave an update on their relationship status.

“We are not officially boyfriend girlfriend yet,” Carl told host Andy Cohen, explaining that he joined the cast during the later half of the season. “I came in late, right? I came in during Casa Amor, so, had a couple weeks to get to know each other.”
Aniya and Carl left the villa at the July 12 finale as the season’s runners-up. Their relationship status had yet to be cemented as their connection was the newest of the final four couples.

Aniya, one of the original cast members, had initially been coupled up with fellow OG cast member KC. However, cracks began to form over time. During the show’s infamously messy Casa Amor episodes at the middle of the season, Aniya, who began to explore a connection with Carl, a bombshell, ultimately chose KC. However, KC explored a connection with bombshell Tierra, with whom he eventually coupled up. Aniya was left single.

In a twist of fate, viewers were invited to vote for two Casa Amor bombshells — one male and one female — who hadn’t been chosen to reenter the villa. Viewers picked Carl, with whom Aniya immediately paired up with once again.

The two spent the last few weeks of the villa sharing some meaningful moments, including meeting one another’s families. During the finale, they were sent on a romantic candlelit and were surprised with a storybook that featured a custom fairytale about their journey together.
“It was always going to be you,” Carl told Aniya during their final moments alone on the show.
During the recent “WWHL” episode, Carl told Cohen that in the two weeks since the islanders have been out of the villa, his connection with Aniya “has just been really strong.”
“We just feel really, really happy,” Carl said. “We just want to kind of keep rolling that as long as we can.”

Season 8 winners Trinity and Bryce — or as the real ones call them, Brinity — are unsurprisingly very much together. The couple, who were the first ones on the show to ever say the three words, “I love you,” confirmed on “WWHL” that they are still inseparable as ever.
The couple joined TODAY on July 15 for their first television appearance after the show wrapped. They told host Craig Melvin that they were dealing with just a touch of “separation anxiety.”

“Something we weren’t anticipating was just like how much our connection has affected us outside of here, too,” Bryce added. “Anytime she’s like, ‘I’m going to go run this errand,’ I’m like, ‘Where’s she going?’ Like, my heart rate starts, I’m like, ‘What’s going on right now?’”

title: Drew Starkey Reacts with Pure Joy at a Surprise Message from DJ Pauly D
summary: Drew Starkey, an unapologetic “Jersey Shore” fan, was surprised with a message from Pauly D during a TODAY appearance on July 30. See the unexpected moment.
story: Drew Starkey, who embraces the “gym, tan and laundry” lifestyle as an unapologetic “Jersey Shore” fan, could not stop smiling when he received a surprise message from his favorite cast member.
The 32-year-old actor stopped by TODAY Thursday, July 30, to chat with Craig Melvin about his new Apple TV series “Lucky” and the upcoming final season of “Outer Banks.”
Toward the end of the interview, Craig playfully mentioned that one of Starkey’s “vices” is his love for reality television.
Starkey confirmed that he is a huge fan of MTV’s “Jersey Shore” and he would love to hang out with star DJ Pauly D one day.
Well, Craig couldn’t make the meet up come true at that moment, but he did have a special gift to reveal: a personal message from the DJ.
